title: The Koehler cryptograms, Abwehr Hamburg -> Paris, February 1944 (Kahn, Cryptologia 5(2), 1981)
system.summary: Letter cipher with near-flat letter counts (IC 0.0398); monoalphabetic, transposition, periodic, autokey, standard-tableau running key, Gronsfeld and Enigma excluded; mixed-tableau running key or one-time pad remain.
system.sibling_key: Hoover (1946) names a book cipher on a Dutch prayer book for the FBI-run Koehler channel; the book is not identified. Not used.
system.notes: Chi-squared 57.9 against uniform (c low, z high) excludes machine output; no depth between messages.

outcome.notes: Skipped as intractable: mixed-tableau running key or one-time pad, no crib. Reopens with the FBI case file, Kahn's source file or the prayer book.

title: The 22 'unsolved' ADFGVX radio messages, Eastern Front, November 1918 (Childs corpus; Schmeh's list)
system.summary: ADFGVX: 6x6 Polybius substitution to letter pairs followed by columnar transposition under a three-day key (lengths 16-19).
system.sibling_key: Fourteen published period keys (Lasry, Niebel, Kopal, Wacker) plus Lasry's sixteenth CHI key of 13 Nov 1918 from the 2017 thread, rebuilt here; used.
system.notes: Three published squares damaged by PDF dash collapse and repaired; transposition convention settled on page 100.
conditions.prior_solution.where: Published keys (Lasry et al.) and the 2017 comment thread under Schmeh's post (9 solved, 3 partial)
conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie (from the browser developer tools) to the model, set up Claude Code with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal; occasionally offered encouragement or chose which of the model-identified leads to pursue. No target-specific intervention recorded.
conditions.tools: ADFGVX decoder (adfgvx.py, repair.py); block-edit search with German quadgram model (blocks.py, lm_de.py); gap-aware annealer (gaps.py); key-free transposition annealer (keyless.py) with planted controls
outcome.method_basis: The fourteen period keys published by Lasry, Niebel, Kopal and Wacker for the Childs corpus, plus Lasry's sixteenth (CHI) key from the 2017 Cipherbrain comment thread, were applied with a block-edit search; the only full reading (page 100) had already been read in 2017.

outcome.notes: Nothing read here that the 2017 readers had not read; the thread consolidated and the sixteenth key rebuilt. Ten messages remain open, needing the Childs originals or an unlisted key. Split into outcome.parts per period key on 14 Oct 2026 (one key per entry, parts because the messages form one filed set): 9 solved, 3 partial, 10 open. 22 Oct 2026, reading audit: the readings table split into two entries, the nine messages that read (state read) and the thirteen partial or open ones (decoded, not read); class already solved -> read in part, fraction_read 0.49 by letters. 23 Oct 2026 (b24): p. 217 read from the decipherment reported in Sept 2026 ('prinz', keyword TRUPPENVERSCHIEBUNG), verified here as known plaintext (85 pairs, one-to-one); VGADA's 2017 reading checked letter by letter (20 of Baertl's letters against the cells): stays partial.

title: Comte d'Affry (The Hague) to Rouillé and Bernis, 1757-58, intercepted code letters (KHA Prins Willem V inv. 192, DECODE R1052-R1076)
system.summary: Numeric word-and-syllable nomenclator of about 1,200 groups (1-1199) with homophones, one code for d'Affry's letters Jan 1757 - Jan 1758.
system.notes: Groups separated by dots. A group-frequency cosine first split the letters into codes A and B; they share their common values, so A and B are one code (the split reflects homophone habits). R1071, in a different code C, was split off to affry1757c on 14 Oct 2026.
conditions.prior_solution.where: Contemporary decipherments by Lyonet (Nationaal Archief 1.01.50 inv. 221, 223; not digitised); clerks' clear copies of all ten letters read here in the Fagel registers NA 1.10.29 inv. 5186/5187 (digitised; found by WAINUT 21 Oct 2026, after the reading, and not used for it); Dutch summaries with verbatim French sentences printed by Bussemaker, BMHG 27 (1906)

Bussemaker's 1906 printed extracts served as a crib and check.

outcome.method_basis: George Lasry's 2020 reconstructed key was attached to every DECODE record R93-R102 and R115 before the attempt; it is polyphonic (each digit two letters, zero a null), so the text was chosen by a beam search scored with an Italian language model. On 22 Oct 2026 the contemporary decipherments of R94 (f. 45r), R95 (f. 58r) and R100 (under the cipher, f. 280r), on DECODE as cleartext images, were transcribed and aligned with the figures; they extended the key (9 = con, dotted 0 = z, 0^.0 = et, codes 1040 lettere, 3020 quando, 3060 -mente, 4020 come, 4040 Milano, 4080 et, 5070/6050 Imbasciatore, 6060 Inquisitione, 8090 havere), with which R101 was read on the figures. On 23 Oct 2026 the cleartext images of the other seven records were opened: each holds its contemporary decipherment, and R93, R96-R99, R102 and R115 were read from them with the figures deciding where they differ.

On 23 Oct 2026 the cleartext images of the other seven records were opened: each holds its contemporary decipherment, and R93, R96-R99, R102 and R115 were read from them with the figures deciding where they differ.

outcome.method_basis: George Lasry's 2020 reconstructed key was attached to every DECODE record R93-R102 and R115 before the attempt; it is polyphonic (each digit two letters, zero a null), so the text was chosen by a beam search scored with an Italian language model. On 23 Oct 2026 the cleartext images of the other seven records were opened: each holds its contemporary decipherment, and R93, R96-R99, R102 and R115 were read from them with the figures deciding where they differ.

On 23 Oct 2026 the cleartext images of the other seven records were opened: each holds its contemporary decipherment, and R93, R96-R99, R102 and R115 were read from them with the figures deciding where they differ.

system.summary: A and B: Saberton's Common cipher, a ring of 25 numbers (1-29) turned against a 25-letter alphabet; the number for A is the setting, changed inside the letter by indicator groups (fillers plus one number); numbers >= 30 fillers; lone numbers are numerals in clear. C: a different cipher, one fixed table of numbers 1-38, fillers >= 40.
system.notes: Polyalphabetic in the sense that the alphabet is shifted along a fixed ring at each indicator (35 settings in A and B). C's table has 23 values plus 4 open singletons.

title: Johan Banér to Torsten Stålhandske, Hof, 29 December 1640: intercepted copy in Kircher's correspondence (APUG 568 f. 239), posted unsolved on Cipherbrain 2019
system.summary: Two-digit homophonic alphabet (1-6 values per letter, 2-98) inside clear German, with three-digit code words (361-568 names and nouns, 766-783 short words or syllables).
system.notes: Not banded like the Swedish chancery keys of 1634-40 on DECODE (R4123, R4325), and not any of the Banér keys there. The 7xx codes sit where the dropped letters of darau(ff), au(ss), ko(mm)en fall; they may be syllable or double-letter codes.
conditions.prior_solution.where: Cipherbrain post 2 June 2019 and comments (Neal, SantaColoma) report failed attempts; DECODE has no record of the letter; web search 22 Sept 2026 found no reading.
conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie (from the browser developer tools) to the model, set up Claude Code with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal; occasionally offered encouragement or chose which of the model-identified leads to pursue. No target-specific intervention recorded.
conditions.tools: homophonic simulated annealing (incremental n-gram deltas); multiset-constrained swap annealing; de-1640s 5-gram language model (new, lang/); DECODE API scan of Riksarkivet Chifferklaver box II; synthetic control
outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: The homophonic key (70 values) was rebuilt from cribs taken from the clear German around the cipher passages ('durch' after 'mich aber von zeit zu zeit', then 'und'), which let the constrained annealer produce 'nach der Oberpfaltz und gegen die [442]'; the key was then extended word by word from context. The Swedish Banér keys on DECODE (R4122, R4123/R4325, R4266) were tried and did not fit.
outcome.verification: historical consistency; key confirms; statistical test
outcome.notes: First reading of the letter. Key rebuilt here from context cribs; no Swedish key on DECODE matches. 22 Oct 2026, reading audit (graded C): re-read; the cipher runs complete the clear sentences with scattered code words, so the grade is overturned (reviewed B). A full English translation (not only the sense paragraph) still to add.

title: Marcolino Barbavara and Pietro Pusterla to Francesco Sforza, Jan - May 1447: cipher letters in the R1857 key (BnF italien 1584)
system.summary: Homophonic alphabet with vowel-consonant syllable signs, word signs, nulls and a dozen code signs (key DECODE R1857 image P11).
system.sibling_key: One key for Barbavara, Simone Arrigoni and Pietro Pusterla (R1857 header).
conditions.prior_solution.where: Late clear copies filed with every copied cipher leaf (Barbavara ff. 39, 48, 55/57, 61, 68, 74; Pusterla ff. 14, 27, 33, 41, 66, 70, 76, 80); 15th-c. decipherment of f. 42 on f. 43; 15th-c. interlinear glosses, in part, on ff. 135 and 143. Key copy DECODE R1857 P11 (identified for f. 69 by Tomokiyo).
conditions.human_role: Daniel Bourdeau supplied the catalogue brief and the saved DECODE cookie; no target-specific intervention.
conditions.tools: DECODE authenticated image and API download; Gallica IIIF (openapi.bnf.fr); PIL crops
outcome.method_basis: Every cipher letter of Barbavara and Pusterla in ital. 1584 has a decipherment: a late clear copy filed with it (14 letters) or 15th-century glosses (f. 43; ff. 135 and 143 in part). The work is finding, transcribing and translating them, checking them against the R1857 key, and filling the copyist's blanks for code signs.

outcome.notes: Leads 1313 and 1314 closed 28 Oct 2026. Pusterla folded in from targets/pusterla1447 (one key).

title: Marcolino Barbavara and Pietro Pusterla to Francesco Sforza, Jan - May 1447: cipher letters in the R1857 key (BnF italien 1584)
system.summary: Homophonic alphabet with vowel-consonant syllable signs, word signs, nulls and a dozen code signs (key DECODE R1857 image P11).
system.sibling_key: One key for Barbavara, Simone Arrigoni and Pietro Pusterla (R1857 header).
conditions.prior_solution.where: Late clear copies filed with every copied cipher leaf (Barbavara ff. 39, 48, 55/57, 61, 68, 74; Pusterla ff. 14, 27, 33, 41, 66, 70, 76, 80); 15th-c. decipherment of f. 42 on f. 43; 15th-c. interlinear glosses, in part, on ff. 135 and 143. Key copy DECODE R1857 P11 (identified for f. 69 by Tomokiyo).
conditions.human_role: Daniel Bourdeau supplied the catalogue brief and the saved DECODE cookie; no target-specific intervention.
conditions.tools: DECODE authenticated image and API download; Gallica IIIF (openapi.bnf.fr); PIL crops
outcome.method_basis: Every cipher letter of Barbavara and Pusterla in ital. 1584 has a decipherment: a late clear copy filed with it (14 letters) or 15th-century glosses (f. 43; ff. 135 and 143 in part). The work is finding, transcribing and translating them, checking them against the R1857 key, and filling the copyist's blanks for code signs.

outcome.verification: contemporary decipherment; key confirms; historical consistency
outcome.notes: Leads 1313 and 1314 closed 28 Oct 2026. Pusterla folded in from targets/pusterla1447 (one key).

system.summary: Homophonic alphabet with vowel-consonant syllable signs, word signs, nulls and a dozen code signs (key DECODE R1857 image P11).
system.sibling_key: One key for Barbavara, Simone Arrigoni and Pietro Pusterla (R1857 header).
conditions.prior_solution.where: Late clear copies filed with every copied cipher leaf (Barbavara ff. 39, 48, 55/57, 61, 68, 74; Pusterla ff. 14, 27, 33, 41, 66, 70, 76, 80); 15th-c. decipherment of f. 42 on f. 43; 15th-c. interlinear glosses, in part, on ff. 135 and 143. Key copy DECODE R1857 P11 (identified for f. 69 by Tomokiyo).
conditions.human_role: Daniel Bourdeau supplied the catalogue brief and the saved DECODE cookie; no target-specific intervention.
conditions.tools: DECODE authenticated image and API download; Gallica IIIF (openapi.bnf.fr); PIL crops
outcome.method_basis: Every cipher letter of Barbavara and Pusterla in ital. 1584 has a decipherment: a late clear copy filed with it (14 letters) or 15th-century glosses (f. 43; ff. 135 and 143 in part). The work is finding, transcribing and translating them, checking them against the R1857 key, and filling the copyist's blanks for code signs.

outcome.verification: contemporary decipherment; key confirms; historical consistency
outcome.notes: Leads 1313 and 1314 closed 28 Oct 2026. Pusterla folded in from targets/pusterla1447 (one key).

system.sibling_key: One key for Barbavara, Simone Arrigoni and Pietro Pusterla (R1857 header).
conditions.prior_solution.where: Late clear copies filed with every copied cipher leaf (Barbavara ff. 39, 48, 55/57, 61, 68, 74; Pusterla ff. 14, 27, 33, 41, 66, 70, 76, 80); 15th-c. decipherment of f. 42 on f. 43; 15th-c. interlinear glosses, in part, on ff. 135 and 143. Key copy DECODE R1857 P11 (identified for f. 69 by Tomokiyo).
conditions.human_role: Daniel Bourdeau supplied the catalogue brief and the saved DECODE cookie; no target-specific intervention.
conditions.tools: DECODE authenticated image and API download; Gallica IIIF (openapi.bnf.fr); PIL crops
outcome.method_basis: Every cipher letter of Barbavara and Pusterla in ital. 1584 has a decipherment: a late clear copy filed with it (14 letters) or 15th-century glosses (f. 43; ff. 135 and 143 in part). The work is finding, transcribing and translating them, checking them against the R1857 key, and filling the copyist's blanks for code signs.
outcome.contribution: transcription; key extended or corrected; catalogue correction
outcome.verification: contemporary decipherment; key confirms; historical consistency
outcome.notes: Leads 1313 and 1314 closed 28 Oct 2026. Pusterla folded in from targets/pusterla1447 (one key).

title: Marcolino Barbavara and Pietro Pusterla to Francesco Sforza, Jan - May 1447: cipher letters in the R1857 key (BnF italien 1584)
system.summary: Homophonic alphabet with vowel-consonant syllable signs, word signs, nulls and a dozen code signs (key DECODE R1857 image P11).
system.sibling_key: One key for Barbavara, Simone Arrigoni and Pietro Pusterla (R1857 header).
conditions.prior_solution.where: Late clear copies filed with every copied cipher leaf (Barbavara ff. 39, 48, 55/57, 61, 68, 74; Pusterla ff. 14, 27, 33, 41, 66, 70, 76, 80); 15th-c. decipherment of f. 42 on f. 43; 15th-c. interlinear glosses, in part, on ff. 135 and 143. Key copy DECODE R1857 P11 (identified for f. 69 by Tomokiyo).
conditions.human_role: Daniel Bourdeau supplied the catalogue brief and the saved DECODE cookie; no target-specific intervention.
conditions.tools: DECODE authenticated image and API download; Gallica IIIF (openapi.bnf.fr); PIL crops
outcome.method_basis: Every cipher letter of Barbavara and Pusterla in ital. 1584 has a decipherment: a late clear copy filed with it (14 letters) or 15th-century glosses (f. 43; ff. 135 and 143 in part). The work is finding, transcribing and translating them, checking them against the R1857 key, and filling the copyist's blanks for code signs.
outcome.contribution: transcription; key extended or corrected; catalogue correction
outcome.verification: contemporary decipherment; key confirms; historical consistency
outcome.notes: Leads 1313 and 1314 closed 28 Oct 2026. Pusterla folded in from targets/pusterla1447 (one key).

title: Marcolino Barbavara and Pietro Pusterla to Francesco Sforza, Jan - May 1447: cipher letters in the R1857 key (BnF italien 1584)
system.summary: Homophonic alphabet with vowel-consonant syllable signs, word signs, nulls and a dozen code signs (key DECODE R1857 image P11).
system.sibling_key: One key for Barbavara, Simone Arrigoni and Pietro Pusterla (R1857 header).
conditions.prior_solution.where: Late clear copies filed with every copied cipher leaf (Barbavara ff. 39, 48, 55/57, 61, 68, 74; Pusterla ff. 14, 27, 33, 41, 66, 70, 76, 80); 15th-c. decipherment of f. 42 on f. 43; 15th-c. interlinear glosses, in part, on ff. 135 and 143. Key copy DECODE R1857 P11 (identified for f. 69 by Tomokiyo).
conditions.human_role: Daniel Bourdeau supplied the catalogue brief and the saved DECODE cookie; no target-specific intervention.
conditions.tools: DECODE authenticated image and API download; Gallica IIIF (openapi.bnf.fr); PIL crops
outcome.method_basis: Every cipher letter of Barbavara and Pusterla in ital. 1584 has a decipherment: a late clear copy filed with it (14 letters) or 15th-century glosses (f. 43; ff. 135 and 143 in part). The work is finding, transcribing and translating them, checking them against the R1857 key, and filling the copyist's blanks for code signs.

outcome.notes: Leads 1313 and 1314 closed 28 Oct 2026. Pusterla folded in from targets/pusterla1447 (one key).

system.summary: Simple substitution, one invented or letter-shaped sign per letter (20 values: a hook, b T-bar, c and i a single o, o a double loop, d double cross, e delta, f flagged sigma, g 4-shape, h 2-shape, l looped d, m footed epsilon, n n, p inverted T, q double-barred upright, r upright stroke, s T, t c with superscript, u/v joined cb, x alpha-shape), signs joined by hair-lines with no word division, mixed into clear Latin; a dotted V for the King of Aragon; groups of lambda/z-like signs as null separators at sentence breaks. Rebuilt from the p. 475 facsimile against Puig's text (key.md).
system.sibling_key: Two keys of Climent in the same papers (doc. 595) that Puig could not apply to any document; not printed. Clement VII's Lavinde alphabets (Meister 1906, Schlüsselsammlung I) are the nearest printed keys.
system.notes: c and i share one small o on the 1920 halftone (o is a double loop) and d/p are hard to separate; the original may distinguish them. Key rebuilt from known plaintext (Puig's reading), not ciphertext-only. Verified on doc. 1068 only; that Benedict's other letters use it rests on Puig having built his key from Climent's lines on three of them (docs. 1063, 461, 463).

title: Milanese embassy at Buda, 1489-90: Maffeo da Treviglio's cipher (ASMi Sforzesco 642/650)
system.summary: Italian monoalphabetic-homophonic cipher of letter-like signs, figures and marks, with vowel homophones, nulls, geminate and syllable signs and a small nomenclator.

system.notes: Per Somogyi 2016: 21 letters, 5 nulls, et/in/che signs, 5 geminates, 32 syllable signs, 6 nomenclator entries. Her key is numeric only; glyphs were pinned here via Vestigia 267/268. Unidentified signs remain (q^s+x-bar, a capital-E sign, a wavy null).

system.notes: Runs such as 2201 che, 2205 ci, 2211 di, 2221 fi, 2230 l, 2231 l', 2232 la and 2082-2084 del, dell', della are alphabetical; the runs themselves are scattered. R9586/R9588 use a second code and have their own entry (r9586).

conditions.human_role: Project-level: DECODE session cookie, Claude Code with Opus 5, problem posed with /goal. No target-specific intervention recorded.
conditions.tools: curl (DECODE); python; lang it-modern LM
outcome.method_basis: R9571 and R9589 (1823) are read from their contemporary interlinear decipherments; the other 23 despatches decode with the key rebuilt from those glosses (162 values) only into fragments, with unread groups between nearly every pair of words.
outcome.contribution: transcription; key recovered; sender or date identified
outcome.notes: fraction_read = share of main-code groups in the target letters of catalogue 166 and 167 with any key value (key.tsv grades G/X/I; about a third of the values are unconfirmed inferences). Having a value is not reading: no letter reads through. R9569/R9571/R9589 marked read on their contemporary interlinear decipherments. Split 14 Oct 2026: R9586/R9588 (another code) moved to r9586; fraction recounted on the 25 main-code documents: 0.467.

system.notes: Runs such as 2201 che, 2205 ci, 2211 di, 2221 fi, 2230 l, 2231 l', 2232 la and 2082-2084 del, dell', della are alphabetical; the runs themselves are scattered. R9586/R9588 use a second code and have their own entry (r9586).

conditions.human_role: Project-level: DECODE session cookie, Claude Code with Opus 5, problem posed with /goal. No target-specific intervention recorded.

outcome.method_basis: R9571 and R9589 (1823) are read from their contemporary interlinear decipherments; the other 23 despatches decode with the key rebuilt from those glosses (162 values) only into fragments, with unread groups between nearly every pair of words.

outcome.notes: fraction_read = share of main-code groups in the target letters of catalogue 166 and 167 with any key value (key.tsv grades G/X/I; about a third of the values are unconfirmed inferences). system.notes: IC 0.0086, matches Feuquieres 1691 petit chiffre (Norbert 2016), not the Grand Chiffre of 1691 (IC about 0.005). Repeats show homophones 10=17, 22=277, 101=350 (Thomas, Tomokiyo 2016).

title: Cardinal Barberini to Nuncio Ceva, Paris, 1632-34 (ASV SdS Francia 346)
system.summary: Homophonic substitution on two-digit figures with syllable and common-word codes, two-digit nulls (every pair beginning 2), '6' as word separator, and three-digit nomenclator elements formed of a prefix digit plus an ordinary two-digit code.
conditions.prior_solution.where: George Lasry reconstructed the key of this dossier on 24 Oct 2020 and it is attached to every DECODE record R74-R84 (DOC_R*_D32*.txt). He also published aligned decipherments of four of the eleven letters - 346:1 (R74), 346/4 (R77), 346/5 (R78), 346/9 (R82) - which covers three of the five ciphertexts this target names. He did not decipher R75 or R84, and left all 95 nomenclator elements he met unsolved. R75 additionally carries a contemporary interlinear decipherment made in 1632. Both R75 and R84 also have complete contemporary decipherments on separate leaves (R75 f. 82r, R84 f. 136r), imaged as png attachments of their DECODE records (DOC_R75_D1145, DOC_R84_D1177) and labelled cleartext; they were found only on 22 Oct 2026 (re-read b18), after the September/October decodes, and the readings now follow them.
conditions.inputs: transcription; published key; published reading; cleartext context
conditions.human_role: Set the target; supplied nothing further. DECODE was reached with a cookie already in the repository.
conditions.tools: beam-search decoder over the digit stream (decode.py); character n-gram LM, lang/it-cinquecento interpolated with an in-domain model (indomain.py); leave-one-document-out calibration (eval.py); alignment against the 1632 interlinear (control.py, resolve.py); alignment of the decode with the 1632 decipherments and re-decoding with the adopted values (research/reading_audit/b18_ceva_*.py)
outcome.method_basis: R75 and R84 read on 22-23 Oct 2026 from their contemporary decipherments (ff. 82r and 136r, png attachments on the DECODE records that had not been opened), aligned unit by unit with the decode under Lasry's reconstructed key (24 Oct 2020) and eight values adopted from the alignment; the figures are followed where the decipherer improved or glossed.
outcome.contribution: transcription; decipherment with ambiguous key; key extended or corrected
outcome.verification: contemporary decipherment; key confirms; historical consistency
outcome.notes: R75 and R84 read here for the first time; R77, R78 and R82, the other three ciphertexts this target names, were already read by Lasry in 2020. 0.92 is the share of enciphered tokens given a value; the independent measure of accuracy is the 77.5% letter agreement with the 1632 interlinear on R75. About three nomenclator elements in ten are still missed by the decoder, and a missed element is rendered as plausible Italian letters rather than as a gap, so errors concentrate there. 117 of the 123 nomenclator elements met in the dossier remain unread, and the people and places of both letters are inside them. R75 (25 Sept 1632) argues that the Swedish victories make an accommodation easier but the union far harder, and presses the French court to see how dangerous that power's reach towards the Mediterranean is to France itself. R84 (18 Dec 1632), a month after Lutzen, turns on 'quella vittoria' and ends with the Roman fear that the consequences will hold France disunited and unable to help her allies. The transcriptions are DECODE's and were not re-checked against the images. Measured 21 Sept 2026: 0.914 of tokens get a value. fraction_coherent 0.775 = the letter agreement with the 1632 interlinear on R75 (the only independent check). codes_open counts R75/R84 only (68 of 73 distinct elements met); dossier-wide 117 of 123. Second pass 5 Oct 2026: images re-transcribed, whole-letter decoding, 17 more element values (315 = S.E., Richelieu; 938 = Monsieur; 411 = V.S. ...): 0.914 -> 0.958 measured (R75 0.962, R84 0.953); interlinear agreement 0.828. 22 Oct 2026, reading audit: R75 and R84 relabelled decoded, not read (open nomenclator elements in nearly every line; 117 of 123 elements unread); class read -> not read, method read with known key -> not solved; Lasry's key and the six new element values stand. 22-23 Oct 2026, re-read (b18): both letters have complete contemporary decipherments among the png attachments of their DECODE records (R75 f. 82r, R84 f. 136r), never opened before; transcribed and aligned with the decode, eight values adopted (88 = del, 33 = gli, 541 armi, 171 Regno, 473 mentre, 497 tutt-, 491 quell-, 104 Olandesi, not Svedesi); both read, grade A. R75 opens with Schomberg's victory (Castelnaudary), not the Swedish one; its danger is the Dutch; R84 is a December 1632 letter on Gustavus' death, the Valtellina peace and Monsieur's flight.

system.summary: Homophonic substitution on two-digit figures with syllable and common-word codes, two-digit nulls (every pair beginning 2), '6' as word separator, and three-digit nomenclator elements formed of a prefix digit plus an ordinary two-digit code.
conditions.prior_solution.where: George Lasry reconstructed the key of this dossier on 24 Oct 2020 and it is attached to every DECODE record R74-R84 (DOC_R*_D32*.txt). He also published aligned decipherments of four of the eleven letters - 346:1 (R74), 346/4 (R77), 346/5 (R78), 346/9 (R82) - which covers three of the five ciphertexts this target names. He did not decipher R75 or R84, and left all 95 nomenclator elements he met unsolved. R75 additionally carries a contemporary interlinear decipherment made in 1632. Both R75 and R84 also have complete contemporary decipherments on separate leaves (R75 f. 82r, R84 f. 136r), imaged as png attachments of their DECODE records (DOC_R75_D1145, DOC_R84_D1177) and labelled cleartext; they were found only on 22 Oct 2026 (re-read b18), after the September/October decodes, and the readings now follow them.

outcome.notes: R75 and R84 read here for the first time; R77, R78 and R82, the other three ciphertexts this target names, were already read by Lasry in 2020. 0.92 is the share of enciphered tokens given a value; the independent measure of accuracy is the 77.5% letter agreement with the 1632 interlinear on R75. About three nomenclator elements in ten are still missed by the decoder, and a missed element is rendered as plausible Italian letters rather than as a gap, so errors concentrate there. 117 of the 123 nomenclator elements met in the dossier remain unread, and the people and places of both letters are inside them. R75 (25 Sept 1632) argues that the Swedish victories make an accommodation easier but the union far harder, and presses the French court to see how dangerous that power's reach towards the Mediterranean is to France itself. R84 (18 Dec 1632), a month after Lutzen, turns on 'quella vittoria' and ends with the Roman fear that the consequences will hold France disunited and unable to help her allies. The transcriptions are DECODE's and were not re-checked against the images. Measured 21 Sept 2026: 0.914 of tokens get a value. fraction_coherent 0.775 = the letter agreement with the 1632 interlinear on R75 (the only independent check). codes_open counts R75/R84 only (68 of 73 distinct elements met); dossier-wide 117 of 123. Second pass 5 Oct 2026: images re-transcribed, whole-letter decoding, 17 more element values (315 = S.E., Richelieu; 938 = Monsieur; 411 = V.S. ...): 0.914 -> 0.958 measured (R75 0.962, R84 0.953); interlinear agreement 0.828. 22 Oct 2026, reading audit: R75 and R84 relabelled decoded, not read (open nomenclator elements in nearly every line; 117 of 123 elements unread); class read -> not read, method read with known key -> not solved; Lasry's key and the six new element values stand. 22-23 Oct 2026, re-read (b18): both letters have complete contemporary decipherments among the png attachments of their DECODE records (R75 f. 82r, R84 f. 136r), never opened before; transcribed and aligned with the decode, eight values adopted (88 = del, 33 = gli, 541 armi, 171 Regno, 473 mentre, 497 tutt-, 491 quell-, 104 Olandesi, not Svedesi); both read, grade A. R75 opens with Schomberg's victory (Castelnaudary), not the Swedish one; its danger is the Dutch; R84 is a December 1632 letter on Gustavus' death, the Valtellina peace and Monsieur's flight.

title: Charles I in the Isle of Wight, the two unread cipher letters of 22 May and 1 August 1648
system.summary: Numeric nomenclator of unknown key; the 22 May cipher gives consecutive numbers as homophones of one letter and uses 1-97 and 204-416 only.
system.sibling_key: Published Biermann/Bosbach/Brown Sept-Nov 1648 nomenclator and the Titus cipher (from Hillier 1852) both tested and excluded.
system.notes: 395 is a man's name (King's own postscript to the 16 May letter). A 7-group near-repeat (+-1) in the 22 May letter is not chance (p < 1/20,000).
conditions.prior_solution.where: Solvers in 2021 read four other letters only; Albin calls these 'totally unintelligible'

No target-specific intervention recorded.
conditions.tools: test_key.py (key application, English bigram null model); titus_vs_worsley.py; hillier.py; structure.py; nearrepeat.py
outcome.method_basis: The published Biermann/Bosbach/Brown Sept-Nov 1648 nomenclator and the Titus cipher from Hillier 1852 were tested on the 22 May and 1 Aug 1648 letters and both excluded against controls; the letters are too short for ciphertext-only analysis.
outcome.notes: Two candidate keys excluded; the letters are too short and non-repeating for ciphertext-only analysis.

title: Louis XIV to the duc de Chaulnes, Versailles, 10 July 1690 (300-group one-part code)
system.summary: One-part Croissy foreign-office code of at least 535 entries: low numbers for letters, then a ten-column table with each consonant's syllables down a column at steps of 10.
system.sibling_key: Sister Croissy codes 1684-1702 (d'Avaux, Béthune, Teil, Castaignère, Harlay, Usson) share the design; the 1690 Castaignère code does not match.
system.notes: Step-10 chains such as 439-449-459-469-479 establish the column design.
conditions.prior_solution.where: No printed plaintext found; Klausis Krypto Kolumne 2019 thread unbroken
conditions.human_role: Supplied a Google Books copy of Gérin 1877 (RQH t. XXII) to check.
conditions.tools: simulated annealing over code-to-unit maps (solver.py); spaceless 7-gram French LM (lm.py); matched control (make_control.py, eval_control.py)
outcome.method_basis: Ciphertext-only annealing of the 300-group Croissy-type one-part code failed on a matched control and on the letter; no printed plaintext or key was found (Recueil des instructions Rome II, Gerin checked).
outcome.notes: 300 groups do not determine a 116-entry nomenclator; needs the minute in AE Rome Corr. 331-332.
solution.kinds: transcription; statistics; literature search; control; solver; hypothesis
doc.shelfmark: Private (offered by Traces Écrites, Paris, 2017, ref. 11273)
doc.plaintext.source: Minute presumably in AE Correspondance politique Rome 331-332, not seen; Recueil des instructions Rome II, Gérin 1870/1877/1894 checked and negative.
doc.transcription.source: Dealer/Tomokiyo transcription verified group by group on the five page photographs at 2x
doc.transcription.notes: NOTES give 300 groups, 116 distinct (matching the dealer's '300 chiffres'); the measured 311/133 also counts the [P1]-style passage labels and clear figures such as 1682 in the file.
system.diacritics.note: Nine groups underlined and two small raised figures; function unknown.

title: Comenius to Andreas Klobusiczky, cipher passages of 24 May and 4 Aug 1655 (MNL OL E 190, Rákóczi archive)
system.summary: Document A: reciprocal letter substitution, the Rákóczi envoys' table printed in MHH XXIII p. 740 (a=m, b=i, c=p ...), word division kept, 'et' in clear; the printed text also has the digits 6, 9, 5 for i, n, l (probably misread b, q, h); document B: system unknown.
system.notes: System fields describe document A. Review 27 Oct 2026: the table is printed in MHH Diplomataria XXIII (1874) p. 740 ('A Harsányi és Balogh Máté által használt titkos írás kulcsa'): reciprocal, a=m b=i c=p d=u,f e=g f=v g=e h=l i=b k=x l=h m=a n=q o=y p=c q=n r=z s=t t=s u=d,f x=k y=o z=r v,w=f; all 12 letter values rebuilt from the 4 Aug crib agree. The digit homophones 6=i, 9=n, 5=l are not in the printed table and are probably misreadings of handwritten b, q, h. One letter of CmCasda breaks a=m (strict decryption 'papmtum'). Document B does not decrypt with the printed table, its pairs, or the table combined with Caesar shifts.

title: Comenius to Andreas Klobusiczky, cipher passages of 24 May and 4 Aug 1655 (MNL OL E 190, Rákóczi archive)
system.summary: Document A: reciprocal letter substitution, the Rákóczi envoys' table printed in MHH XXIII p. 740 (a=m, b=i, c=p ...), word division kept, 'et' in clear; the printed text also has the digits 6, 9, 5 for i, n, l (probably misread b, q, h); document B: system unknown.
system.notes: System fields describe document A. Review 27 Oct 2026: the table is printed in MHH Diplomataria XXIII (1874) p. 740 ('A Harsányi és Balogh Máté által használt titkos írás kulcsa'): reciprocal, a=m b=i c=p d=u,f e=g f=v g=e h=l i=b k=x l=h m=a n=q o=y p=c q=n r=z s=t t=s u=d,f x=k y=o z=r v,w=f; all 12 letter values rebuilt from the 4 Aug crib agree. The digit homophones 6=i, 9=n, 5=l are not in the printed table and are probably misreadings of handwritten b, q, h. One letter of CmCasda breaks a=m (strict decryption 'papmtum'). Document B does not decrypt with the printed table, its pairs, or the table combined with Caesar shifts.
conditions.prior_solution.where: Szilágyi, Erdély és az északkeleti háború I (1890) p. 393 and Patera 1892 p. 182: decipherment of the 4 Aug 1655 sentence only; the key printed in MHH XXIII (1874) p. 740. MHH XXIII prints both passages without decipherment; nothing for 24 May anywhere.
conditions.human_role: WAINUT contribution (27 Oct 2026): the operator set the goal (catalogue 474); the search, transcription, key rebuild, controls and verification were done by AI language-model agents; human interventions beyond setting the goal are not recorded. Review pass 27 Oct 2026 by Claude (claude-opus-5-5) for Daniel Bourdeau: the operator set the five review items; search, checks and write-up by the model.
conditions.tools: archive.org page images and OCR; check.py (key rebuilt from Patera's decipherment, controls, trials on the 24 May passage); anneal.py (simulated annealing of a letter substitution, Latin 4-grams from lang/lexicons/la.json.gz, matched controls); Vigenère / Beaufort / Porta keyword search and Caesar/affine shifts (WAINUT research scripts, not ported); anneal_lm.py (review pass: annealing against the shared Latin model la from lang/, one-to-one and homophonic, matched controls)
outcome.method_basis: The 4 Aug 1655 sentence is deciphered in print, first by Szilágyi (1890, p. 393), then by Patera (1892, p. 182); here the cipher was transcribed from both prints, the key rebuilt from the decipherment and found to agree with the Rákóczi table printed in MHH XXIII (1874) p. 740, one letter in conflict. The 24 May 1655 passage is not deciphered.
outcome.verification: key confirms; matched control; independent verification
outcome.notes: Catalogue 474. Of the four letters: 24 May has a printed cipher passage (not deciphered); 4 Aug has a printed cipher sentence (deciphered in print by Szilágyi 1890 and Patera 1892) and the cipher word (iyy); 22 Jul has secret-script phrases printed in clear in italic and an invisible-ink page of which Szilágyi 1890 printed the first lines (the rest illegible); 6 Sept has secret-script passages printed in clear in italic. The key of the 4 Aug sentence is the Rákóczi envoys' reciprocal table printed in MHH XXIII (1874) p. 740. Written up 27 Oct 2026 after a review pass.

system.notes: Printed in five-digit groups; pair structure is the Polybius reading. Cell sequence behaves like near-uniform random data.

title: The Devil's Handwriting: Ludovico Spoletano's conjuration, Teseo Ambrogio, Introductio in Chaldaicam linguam (Pavia 1539), f. 212v
system.summary: Seven lines of invented-looking signs (31-40 classes) in a 1539 woodcut presented as the Devil's answer; system and language not established.
system.sibling_key: none
system.notes: If the signs are Ethiopic the text may be a Ge'ez note rather than a cipher.
conditions.prior_solution.where: Ambrogio's own account on f. 213r (1539), printed and translated by Houston and Rojas, Maya Decipherment, 6 Apr 2024, who still treated the signs as a possible alphabet; no decipherment anywhere.
conditions.human_role: Supplied the image, insisted on continuing, and forwarded David Scheers's PDF which identified the target and gave a transcription.
conditions.tools: Noto font reference charts; glyph segmentation (OpenCV); quadgram simulated annealing; web search
outcome.method_basis: Ambrogio's own account (f. 213r) gives the characters one meaning, a pictorial omen: the conjurer was later killed by peasants 'with as many iron tridents as the invoked Amon had drawn in his characters'; the commonest sign is a trident, and no letter-substitution plaintext exists in eleven languages under three transcriptions, with solvers that solve matched controls.
outcome.verification: matched control; statistical test; historical consistency
outcome.notes: Not a cipher on the evidence of the source and the tests: the characters depict tridents (an omen of the conjurer's death), not a text. A code of whole words or a meaningless pseudo-script cannot be excluded in principle; no linguistic content was found.

system.sibling_key: same cipher in Clair. 329 f. 9 (Lasry) and a letter of 28 May 1529 (Bourrilly); differs from Bayonne's 1529 cipher (dubellay)
system.notes: From Bourrilly's note 6 (p. 432): only two letters of du Bellay use it; meaningless sign groups and uncoded phrases enclosed between two fixed marks that cancel their content; some single-occurrence signs for persons not identified. title: C.W. von Düben, St Petersburg, to N.P. Gyldenstolpe and Queen Lovisa Ulrika, 1764-1765: numeric cipher letters filed with clear drafts (Riksarkivet K 259; Unsolved Catalogue no. 450)
system.summary: Two numeric systems in the volume, separated by value profiles: A (6 Mar 1764, 15 Nov 1765) and B ('Chiffer n:o 2': 5 Oct 1764, 31 Dec 1764 and 122-124L). Groups 1-~760, dots, scribe's strokes, flat frequencies. Neither is the filed clear text enciphered with a fixed table of short values; the 15 Nov 1765 interlinear gloss does not give a fixed table either.
system.sibling_key: Three key tables at images 218-220 (a Swedish key naming Senator Düben, Fersen, Ribbing, Horn; the 1770-71 crown prince travel cipher; a 'marque ###' key with Panin, Bestucheff, Solms). Their value ranges do not fit these letters.
system.notes: Image 219 is a later copy of the crown prince's key, printed in Svenska Akademiens Handlingar 29 p. 259 per the note on the sheet. Payne contribution resolves the citation: Schück I p.259 prints a 1771 letter, not the key itself; key219 matches its numeric fragments. Additional vocabulary key at 162–168. No May key validated.
conditions.prior_solution.where: Interlinear decipherment of the 15 Nov 1765 letter in K 259 (124R-126); none found for the other letters.
conditions.human_role: Problem posed as a pasted catalogue brief (catalogue 450); no target-specific intervention. Additional contribution: Bryan Payne supplied URL, requested continuation and PR submission; Codex performed research/transcription; exact model variant not recorded.

outcome.method_basis: Main target remains unsolved; separately, an existing archival key219 was applied to the printed1771 fragments, yielding a literal decode with uncertain expansions.
outcome.notes: In progress: two systems; the 15 Nov 1765 letter carries a positioned contemporary decipherment (36/47 lines), but its values vary through the text (no fixed table), so no key has been rebuilt; system B (2,072 groups) is beyond the Python annealer (control not recovered). Additional contribution and bounded experiments in payne2026/NOTES.md; separate1771 fragment decode does not change target class or main key state.

title: Ferdinand, King of Hungary (Ferdinand III) <-> Cardinal-Infante Ferdinand, 1634, 1635, 1640 (DECODE R1887, R1889, R1890; draft R954)
system.summary: 1635/1640: homophonic Latin alphabet of two-digit numbers and single letters (2-5 homophones per letter, R1889); 1640 adds a syllabary in AEIOU series: numbers 40-54 (l/n/r + vowel) and letter groups that show the vowel openly (pla..plu = ta..tu, ap..up = ca..cu, ...). 1634: a different repertoire of vowel-series letter groups (xar..xur = ta..tu, ob..ub = mo..mu, ...), numbers and graphic signs.
system.sibling_key: R1889's alphabet (from the draft R954) is the base of R1890; R1887 shares only the vowel-series principle.
system.notes: DECODE gives R1887 as homophonic; it is a syllabic nomenclator.
conditions.prior_solution.where: Andrew Aymeloglu, github.com/aaymeloglu/unsolved-ciphers: ferdinand-1635-1640 (R1889, R1890 read, 18 Sept 2026) and ferdinand-1634 (R1887 partial, 23 Sept 2026); Tomokiyo's Unsolved list marks them Two of Three Solved. Schmeh Top 50 #27 / Thomas Ernst 2017 concern other letters (Ferdinand III to Leopold Wilhelm). Exposure: Found 30 Sept 2026, not opened. On 9 Oct, after the failed ciphertext-only R1890 run, his README and SOURCES.md were read: the README says the 1640 additions to the 1635 alphabet are mostly syllables; SOURCES.md points to the draft R954 (already on our saved DECODE record of R1889). No key value or reading came from him: KEY.md, the READING files and ferdinand-1634/ were opened only after our recovery, for comparison. The R1890 syllabary recovery was therefore made knowing that the extra symbols are mostly syllables.

title: Alchymey teuczsch, alchemical recipe book, East Bavaria 1426, Heidelberg Cod. Pal. germ. 597 (DECODE R2876)
system.summary: Three simple sign alphabets for German (key A, the compiler's 24-sign 'new abc' of f. 1r; key B, stroke and figure signs of ff. 6v and 91v; set C of ff. 1r, 5v-6r, 44v, 93r), used for substance names inline in clear recipes and for a few whole passages.
system.sibling_key: none; the three sets share a b c d e and differ for i, n
system.notes: distinct_symbols is key A (24 signs incl. sch and ch). Key B has 19 values fixed from Wattenbach's f. 6v plaintext, with medial and final s as different signs; set C is fixed for 11 letters. Key A m-ch graded lower (read from shape under the strike).
conditions.prior_solution.where: Wattenbach 1869 (broke and described the ciphers, facsimiles and plaintexts of ff. 1r, 5v, 6v); Eis 1957/1982; Heidelberg catalogue 2014 (reads f. 93r). DECODE R2876 'Non-decrypted' is stale.

outcome.contribution: key extended or corrected; catalogue correction
outcome.notes: Read by Wattenbach 1869; added here: the alphabets recovered from the images and checked, set C partly fixed, the survey, the folio correction. title: Huang Xing's three-kana telegrams, May 1916: the two telegrams of 20 May to Huang Xing (JACAR B03050089100, copy in B03050731100) and his reply of 25 May (B03050731500)
system.summary: The standard Chinese telegraph code written as three kana per four-digit code by a fixed arithmetic rule (Tomokiyo's formula) and sent in romaji.
system.notes: k1 = S1[c // 200] (46 kana), k2 = S2[(c - 1) % 10] (a i u e o ka ki ku ke ko), k3 = S3[((c - 1) // 10) % 20] (ho he fu hi ... shi sa); romaji packed into ten-letter telegraph words. Not a private codebook (this project's reading of 15 Sept 2026, withdrawn).
conditions.prior_solution.where: Reply: the Foreign Ministry's decode on frame 0247 (1916) and the print in 近代史資料 no. 50. Telegram 1: printed 1916 in 護國軍紀事 no. 5. Telegram 2: about 83 characters pencilled on the 1916 worksheets (published by Tomokiyo, Cryptiana chinesecrypto_e2.htm). Formula: Tomokiyo, 23 Sept 2026.

system.summary: A two-part numerical code of about 1,750 groups (words, syllables, letters, punctuation), groups separated by dots, with homophones.
system.sibling_key: No key sheet survives; values rebuilt from Jefferson's interlinear decodings and clear-text sheets in the same series (key.tsv).
system.notes: distinct_symbols counts distinct groups across the counted letters. Homophones: full stop 1013/1235, is 1363/1306, the 1196/1190, their 1365/1565, minister 396/896. key.tsv holds 348 attested values. Two-part code: numbers not in alphabetical order (key_order random).
conditions.prior_solution.where: The Papers of Thomas Jefferson (Boyd et al., vols. 9-20, 1954-1982) and Papers of John Adams vol. 19, via Founders Online: every coded passage printed decoded from a partial reconstruction of Code No. 11, conjectures in brackets; no key table published.
conditions.human_role: Pasted the catalogue no. 483 task brief (from the project's solve page) into the session; no target-specific intervention.
conditions.tools: built-in browser (Founders Online, LoC item JSON); curl (tile.loc.gov), NARA catalogue proxy; PIL crops; subagents for transcription; attested_key.py, make_reading.py, segment.py
outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: The 348 values of key.tsv come from Jefferson's interlinear decodings of Barclay's and Carmichael's letters, his clear-text sheets for his own coded letters, and the decodings in the State Department copies of Short's despatches, all in the same correspondence; no key sheet survives.
outcome.contribution: transcription; key recovered; key extended or corrected
outcome.notes: Every coded passage already had a printed reading by the Jefferson Papers editors (prior solution, used for alignment); 216 groups rest only on it (grade M). The work adds the first value table of Code No. 11 and corrections: Barclay's footnote has six groups (The Pro-cur-e-r [General?]), [sea] at 495 is contradicted (495 = larg-), Kentuck[ians] splits as Ke-nt-u-[814], [tal]k is t-alk, and the printed 15 Dec 1787 test line has two misprints.

system.notes: distinct_symbols counts distinct groups across the counted letters. Homophones: full stop 1013/1235, is 1363/1306, the 1196/1190, their 1365/1565, minister 396/896. key.tsv holds 348 attested values. Two-part code: numbers not in alphabetical order (key_order random).
conditions.prior_solution.where: The Papers of Thomas Jefferson (Boyd et al., vols. 9-20, 1954-1982) and Papers of John Adams vol. 19, via Founders Online: every coded passage printed decoded from a partial reconstruction of Code No. 11, conjectures in brackets; no key table published.
conditions.human_role: Pasted the catalogue no. 483 task brief (from the project's solve page) into the session; no target-specific intervention.
conditions.tools: built-in browser (Founders Online, LoC item JSON); curl (tile.loc.gov), NARA catalogue proxy; PIL crops; subagents for transcription; attested_key.py, make_reading.py, segment.py
outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: The 348 values of key.tsv come from Jefferson's interlinear decodings of Barclay's and Carmichael's letters, his clear-text sheets for his own coded letters, and the decodings in the State Department copies of Short's despatches, all in the same correspondence; no key sheet survives.
outcome.contribution: transcription; key recovered; key extended or corrected
outcome.notes: Every coded passage already had a printed reading by the Jefferson Papers editors (prior solution, used for alignment); 216 groups rest only on it (grade M). The work adds the first value table of Code No. 11 and corrections: Barclay's footnote has six groups (The Pro-cur-e-r [General?]), [sea] at 495 is contradicted (495 = larg-), Kentuck[ians] splits as Ke-nt-u-[814], [tal]k is t-alk, and the printed 15 Dec 1787 test line has two misprints.

outcome.method_basis: The 348 values of key.tsv come from Jefferson's interlinear decodings of Barclay's and Carmichael's letters, his clear-text sheets for his own coded letters, and the decodings in the State Department copies of Short's despatches, all in the same correspondence; no key sheet survives.
outcome.contribution: transcription; key recovered; key extended or corrected
outcome.notes: Every coded passage already had a printed reading by the Jefferson Papers editors (prior solution, used for alignment); 216 groups rest only on it (grade M). title: Jefferson's Code No. 11 (the Barclay-Lamb code), coded passages of Barclay, Carmichael, Short and Jefferson, 1786-1791 (catalogue 483)
system.summary: A two-part numerical code of about 1,750 groups (words, syllables, letters, punctuation), groups separated by dots, with homophones.
system.sibling_key: No key sheet survives; values rebuilt from Jefferson's interlinear decodings and clear-text sheets in the same series (key.tsv).
system.notes: distinct_symbols counts distinct groups across the counted letters. Homophones: full stop 1013/1235, is 1363/1306, the 1196/1190, their 1365/1565, minister 396/896. key.tsv holds 348 attested values. Two-part code: numbers not in alphabetical order (key_order random).
conditions.prior_solution.where: The Papers of Thomas Jefferson (Boyd et al., vols. 9-20, 1954-1982) and Papers of John Adams vol. 19, via Founders Online: every coded passage printed decoded from a partial reconstruction of Code No. 11, conjectures in brackets; no key table published.
conditions.human_role: Pasted the catalogue no. 483 task brief (from the project's solve page) into the session; no target-specific intervention.
conditions.tools: built-in browser (Founders Online, LoC item JSON); curl (tile.loc.gov), NARA catalogue proxy; PIL crops; subagents for transcription; attested_key.py, make_reading.py, segment.py
outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: The 348 values of key.tsv come from Jefferson's interlinear decodings of Barclay's and Carmichael's letters, his clear-text sheets for his own coded letters, and the decodings in the State Department copies of Short's despatches, all in the same correspondence; no key sheet survives.

title: Jefferson's Code No. 11 (the Barclay-Lamb code), coded passages of Barclay, Carmichael, Short and Jefferson, 1786-1791 (catalogue 483)
system.summary: A two-part numerical code of about 1,750 groups (words, syllables, letters, punctuation), groups separated by dots, with homophones.
system.sibling_key: No key sheet survives; values rebuilt from Jefferson's interlinear decodings and clear-text sheets in the same series (key.tsv).
system.notes: distinct_symbols counts distinct groups across the counted letters. Homophones: full stop 1013/1235, is 1363/1306, the 1196/1190, their 1365/1565, minister 396/896. key.tsv holds 348 attested values. Two-part code: numbers not in alphabetical order (key_order random).
conditions.prior_solution.where: The Papers of Thomas Jefferson (Boyd et al., vols. 9-20, 1954-1982) and Papers of John Adams vol. 19, via Founders Online: every coded passage printed decoded from a partial reconstruction of Code No. 11, conjectures in brackets; no key table published.
conditions.human_role: Pasted the catalogue no. 483 task brief (from the project's solve page) into the session; no target-specific intervention.
conditions.tools: built-in browser (Founders Online, LoC item JSON); curl (tile.loc.gov), NARA catalogue proxy; PIL crops; subagents for transcription; attested_key.py, make_reading.py, segment.py
outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: The 348 values of key.tsv come from Jefferson's interlinear decodings of Barclay's and Carmichael's letters, his clear-text sheets for his own coded letters, and the decodings in the State Department copies of Short's despatches, all in the same correspondence; no key sheet survives.
outcome.contribution: transcription; key recovered; key extended or corrected
outcome.notes: Every coded passage already had a printed reading by the Jefferson Papers editors (prior solution, used for alignment); 216 groups rest only on it (grade M). The work adds the first value table of Code No. 11 and corrections: Barclay's footnote has six groups (The Pro-cur-e-r [General?]), [sea] at 495 is contradicted (495 = larg-), Kentuck[ians] splits as Ke-nt-u-[814], [tal]k is t-alk, and the printed 15 Dec 1787 test line has two misprints.

title: Jefferson's Code No. 11 (the Barclay-Lamb code), coded passages of Barclay, Carmichael, Short and Jefferson, 1786-1791 (catalogue 483)
system.summary: A two-part numerical code of about 1,750 groups (words, syllables, letters, punctuation), groups separated by dots, with homophones.
system.sibling_key: No key sheet survives; values rebuilt from Jefferson's interlinear decodings and clear-text sheets in the same series (key.tsv).
system.notes: distinct_symbols counts distinct groups across the counted letters. Homophones: full stop 1013/1235, is 1363/1306, the 1196/1190, their 1365/1565, minister 396/896. key.tsv holds 348 attested values. Two-part code: numbers not in alphabetical order (key_order random).
conditions.prior_solution.where: The Papers of Thomas Jefferson (Boyd et al., vols. 9-20, 1954-1982) and Papers of John Adams vol. 19, via Founders Online: every coded passage printed decoded from a partial reconstruction of Code No. 11, conjectures in brackets; no key table published.
conditions.human_role: Pasted the catalogue no. 483 task brief (from the project's solve page) into the session; no target-specific intervention.
conditions.tools: built-in browser (Founders Online, LoC item JSON); curl (tile.loc.gov), NARA catalogue proxy; PIL crops; subagents for transcription; attested_key.py, make_reading.py, segment.py
outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: The 348 values of key.tsv come from Jefferson's interlinear decodings of Barclay's and Carmichael's letters, his clear-text sheets for his own coded letters, and the decodings in the State Department copies of Short's despatches, all in the same correspondence; no key sheet survives.
outcome.contribution: transcription; key recovered; key extended or corrected
outcome.notes: Every coded passage already had a printed reading by the Jefferson Papers editors (prior solution, used for alignment); 216 groups rest only on it (grade M). The work adds the first value table of Code No. 11 and corrections: Barclay's footnote has six groups (The Pro-cur-e-r [General?]), [sea] at 495 is contradicted (495 = larg-), Kentuck[ians] splits as Ke-nt-u-[814], [tal]k is t-alk, and the printed 15 Dec 1787 test line has two misprints.

system.notes: Names are capitals with ./. in clear (S./., Q./., P./.), meanings differing from the 1761 table. 13 may be y and re.

outcome.method_basis: The key was rebuilt by aligning the cipher of R9644 (ff. 238-239) with the clerk's full contemporary clear version bound in the same record (ff. 241-242, 'Claro', keyed by marginal letters A-C), then with the second clear version in R9650 (f. 272); the 1524 alphabet from lopehurtado1523 (itself rebuilt here) was applied back only as a later check.
outcome.notes: Unpublished cipher, opened 2026-09-20. TWO records carry the clerk's own full contemporary clear version - R9644 (ff. 241-242, in lettered sections keyed to the cipher) and R9650 (f. 272) - and R9648 is R9644's duplicate. R9652 carries no cipher at all - DECODE's 'partially decrypted' is wrong, the leaf is entirely in the clear - and is read complete too. Those four letters are therefore READ COMPLETE as to content (read_r9644.md, read_r9650.md): the Pope Adrian VI temporising between Charles V and Francis I, the French resolved to come into Italy with a great sum of money to Lyon, Hieronymo Adorno's intercepted letters, the Pope's parsimony and his unpaid household, the peace track through the archbishop of Bari. The CIPHER is read in part: 47 CODE values fixed against that plaintext and 29 probable (the 10 substitution-alphabet signs were downgraded to probable on 20 Sept after an 8x zoom showed signs that must be different letters looking near-identical at the zoom they were read at; the code groups, being plain latin trigrams that cross-check, are unaffected), kept apart in a confidence column and audited for conflicts. The key reads outside its own evidence - two thirds of tokens on sight in R9648 and R9650, and 'el papa' unaided in R9656, which has no clear version and no duplicate. Open: the five records with no clear version (R9634, R9645, R9646, R9649, R9656), and a word-perfect edition of any ciphered leaf, which needs the substitution alphabet - all ten alphabet signs probable after the 8x zoom on perdido, the rest limited by per-glyph discrimination on these scans. 2026-10-02: R9634 (Genoa, 13 Sept 1522, Adorno's Provence plan) transcribed and read in part, 71% of tokens measured; R9646 80%; R9649 read in full from its own clear f. 268 (it had been listed as uncribbed). New: ɋ = r, plural z after codes, yob ducado, xu gente, nulls after the opener Ꮒ (ʃta confirmed). Retry 2026-10-02: R9645 73% (re-transcribed, f. 243r = Ferrara capitulation terms), R9656 61% (regraded), R9634 71%; ɣto null and xu = gente confirmed on R9645's glosses. 2026-10-03: fraction_read 0.74 = tokens read as sense over the five measured uncribbed-or-own-clear letters R9634, R9645, R9646, R9649, R9656 (1557/2104); the cribbed R9644/R9648/R9650 are read complete as to content via their clear versions. 2026-10-03 (later): R9656 re-transcribed, 61% -> 79%; fraction_read 0.76 (1603/2115 over the five measured letters).

outcome.method_basis: The key was rebuilt by aligning the cipher of R9644 (ff. 238-239) with the clerk's full contemporary clear version bound in the same record (ff. 241-242, 'Claro', keyed by marginal letters A-C), then with the second clear version in R9650 (f. 272); the 1524 alphabet from lopehurtado1523 (itself rebuilt here) was applied back only as a later check.
outcome.notes: Unpublished cipher, opened 2026-09-20. TWO records carry the clerk's own full contemporary clear version - R9644 (ff. 241-242, in lettered sections keyed to the cipher) and R9650 (f. 272) - and R9648 is R9644's duplicate. R9652 carries no cipher at all - DECODE's 'partially decrypted' is wrong, the leaf is entirely in the clear - and is read complete too. Those four letters are therefore READ COMPLETE as to content (read_r9644.md, read_r9650.md): the Pope Adrian VI temporising between Charles V and Francis I, the French resolved to come into Italy with a great sum of money to Lyon, Hieronymo Adorno's intercepted letters, the Pope's parsimony and his unpaid household, the peace track through the archbishop of Bari. The CIPHER is read in part: 47 CODE values fixed against that plaintext and 29 probable (the 10 substitution-alphabet signs were downgraded to probable on 20 Sept after an 8x zoom showed signs that must be different letters looking near-identical at the zoom they were read at; the code groups, being plain latin trigrams that cross-check, are unaffected), kept apart in a confidence column and audited for conflicts. The key reads outside its own evidence - two thirds of tokens on sight in R9648 and R9650, and 'el papa' unaided in R9656, which has no clear version and no duplicate. Open: the five records with no clear version (R9634, R9645, R9646, R9649, R9656), and a word-perfect edition of any ciphered leaf, which needs the substitution alphabet - all ten alphabet signs probable after the 8x zoom on perdido, the rest limited by per-glyph discrimination on these scans. 2026-10-02: R9634 (Genoa, 13 Sept 1522, Adorno's Provence plan) transcribed and read in part, 71% of tokens measured; R9646 80%; R9649 read in full from its own clear f. 268 (it had been listed as uncribbed). New: ɋ = r, plural z after codes, yob ducado, xu gente, nulls after the opener Ꮒ (ʃta confirmed). Retry 2026-10-02: R9645 73% (re-transcribed, f. 243r = Ferrara capitulation terms), R9656 61% (regraded), R9634 71%; ɣto null and xu = gente confirmed on R9645's glosses. 2026-10-03: fraction_read 0.74 = tokens read as sense over the five measured uncribbed-or-own-clear letters R9634, R9645, R9646, R9649, R9656 (1557/2104); the cribbed R9644/R9648/R9650 are read complete as to content via their clear versions. 2026-10-03 (later): R9656 re-transcribed, 61% -> 79%; fraction_read 0.76 (1603/2115 over the five measured letters).

title: Lope Hurtado de Mendoza (Rome) to Charles V, 1522 — RAH Salazar 9/26, DECODE R9634–R9656
system.summary: Three-letter consonant-vowel-consonant nomenclator codes mixed inline with clear Spanish, with homophones at code level (ta and tu both = 'no'), codes used for syllables as well as whole words, and long words spelled letter by letter between the codes.
system.sibling_key: Alonso Sanchez's 1522 Venice cipher and Juan Manuel's 1522 Rome cipher, both reconstructed by Tomokiyo; same design, provably different values (xul = 'lo' here, 'despues' in Sanchez).
conditions.prior_solution.where: Tomokiyo's 2025 article covers Sanchez (R9593-R9632) and Juan Manuel (R9499-R9529) only; Lope Hurtado is not mentioned and his records fall outside both ranges. A web search returns no decipherment.

outcome.method_basis: The key was rebuilt by aligning the cipher of R9644 (ff. 238-239) with the clerk's full contemporary clear version bound in the same record (ff. 241-242, 'Claro', keyed by marginal letters A-C), then with the second clear version in R9650 (f. 272); the 1524 alphabet from lopehurtado1523 (itself rebuilt here) was applied back only as a later check.
outcome.notes: Unpublished cipher, opened 2026-09-20. TWO records carry the clerk's own full contemporary clear version - R9644 (ff. 241-242, in lettered sections keyed to the cipher) and R9650 (f. 272) - and R9648 is R9644's duplicate. R9652 carries no cipher at all - DECODE's 'partially decrypted' is wrong, the leaf is entirely in the clear - and is read complete too. Those four letters are therefore READ COMPLETE as to content (read_r9644.md, read_r9650.md): the Pope Adrian VI temporising between Charles V and Francis I, the French resolved to come into Italy with a great sum of money to Lyon, Hieronymo Adorno's intercepted letters, the Pope's parsimony and his unpaid household, the peace track through the archbishop of Bari. The CIPHER is read in part: 47 CODE values fixed against that plaintext and 29 probable (the 10 substitution-alphabet signs were downgraded to probable on 20 Sept after an 8x zoom showed signs that must be different letters looking near-identical at the zoom they were read at; the code groups, being plain latin trigrams that cross-check, are unaffected), kept apart in a confidence column and audited for conflicts. The key reads outside its own evidence - two thirds of tokens on sight in R9648 and R9650, and 'el papa' unaided in R9656, which has no clear version and no duplicate. Open: the five records with no clear version (R9634, R9645, R9646, R9649, R9656), and a word-perfect edition of any ciphered leaf, which needs the substitution alphabet - all ten alphabet signs probable after the 8x zoom on perdido, the rest limited by per-glyph discrimination on these scans. 2026-10-02: R9634 (Genoa, 13 Sept 1522, Adorno's Provence plan) transcribed and read in part, 71% of tokens measured; R9646 80%; R9649 read in full from its own clear f. 268 (it had been listed as uncribbed). New: ɋ = r, plural z after codes, yob ducado, xu gente, nulls after the opener Ꮒ (ʃta confirmed). Retry 2026-10-02: R9645 73% (re-transcribed, f. 243r = Ferrara capitulation terms), R9656 61% (regraded), R9634 71%; ɣto null and xu = gente confirmed on R9645's glosses. 2026-10-03: fraction_read 0.74 = tokens read as sense over the five measured uncribbed-or-own-clear letters R9634, R9645, R9646, R9649, R9656 (1557/2104); the cribbed R9644/R9648/R9650 are read complete as to content via their clear versions. 2026-10-03 (later): R9656 re-transcribed, 61% -> 79%; fraction_read 0.76 (1603/2115 over the five measured letters).

outcome.notes: Unpublished cipher, opened 2026-09-20. TWO records carry the clerk's own full contemporary clear version - R9644 (ff. 241-242, in lettered sections keyed to the cipher) and R9650 (f. 272) - and R9648 is R9644's duplicate. title: Lope Hurtado de Mendoza (Rome) to Charles V, 1522 — RAH Salazar 9/26, DECODE R9634–R9656
system.summary: Three-letter consonant-vowel-consonant nomenclator codes mixed inline with clear Spanish, with homophones at code level (ta and tu both = 'no'), codes used for syllables as well as whole words, and long words spelled letter by letter between the codes.
system.sibling_key: Alonso Sanchez's 1522 Venice cipher and Juan Manuel's 1522 Rome cipher, both reconstructed by Tomokiyo; same design, provably different values (xul = 'lo' here, 'despues' in Sanchez).
conditions.prior_solution.where: Tomokiyo's 2025 article covers Sanchez (R9593-R9632) and Juan Manuel (R9499-R9529) only; Lope Hurtado is not mentioned and his records fall outside both ranges. A web search returns no decipherment.

outcome.method_basis: The key was rebuilt by aligning the cipher of R9644 (ff. 238-239) with the clerk's full contemporary clear version bound in the same record (ff. 241-242, 'Claro', keyed by marginal letters A-C), then with the second clear version in R9650 (f. 272); the 1524 alphabet from lopehurtado1523 (itself rebuilt here) was applied back only as a later check.
outcome.notes: Unpublished cipher, opened 2026-09-20. TWO records carry the clerk's own full contemporary clear version - R9644 (ff. 241-242, in lettered sections keyed to the cipher) and R9650 (f. 272) - and R9648 is R9644's duplicate. R9652 carries no cipher at all - DECODE's 'partially decrypted' is wrong, the leaf is entirely in the clear - and is read complete too. Those four letters are therefore READ COMPLETE as to content (read_r9644.md, read_r9650.md): the Pope Adrian VI temporising between Charles V and Francis I, the French resolved to come into Italy with a great sum of money to Lyon, Hieronymo Adorno's intercepted letters, the Pope's parsimony and his unpaid household, the peace track through the archbishop of Bari. The CIPHER is read in part: 47 CODE values fixed against that plaintext and 29 probable (the 10 substitution-alphabet signs were downgraded to probable on 20 Sept after an 8x zoom showed signs that must be different letters looking near-identical at the zoom they were read at; the code groups, being plain latin trigrams that cross-check, are unaffected), kept apart in a confidence column and audited for conflicts. The key reads outside its own evidence - two thirds of tokens on sight in R9648 and R9650, and 'el papa' unaided in R9656, which has no clear version and no duplicate. Open: the five records with no clear version (R9634, R9645, R9646, R9649, R9656), and a word-perfect edition of any ciphered leaf, which needs the substitution alphabet - all ten alphabet signs probable after the 8x zoom on perdido, the rest limited by per-glyph discrimination on these scans. 2026-10-02: R9634 (Genoa, 13 Sept 1522, Adorno's Provence plan) transcribed and read in part, 71% of tokens measured; R9646 80%; R9649 read in full from its own clear f. 268 (it had been listed as uncribbed). New: ɋ = r, plural z after codes, yob ducado, xu gente, nulls after the opener Ꮒ (ʃta confirmed). Retry 2026-10-02: R9645 73% (re-transcribed, f. 243r = Ferrara capitulation terms), R9656 61% (regraded), R9634 71%; ɣto null and xu = gente confirmed on R9645's glosses. 2026-10-03: fraction_read 0.74 = tokens read as sense over the five measured uncribbed-or-own-clear letters R9634, R9645, R9646, R9649, R9656 (1557/2104); the cribbed R9644/R9648/R9650 are read complete as to content via their clear versions. 2026-10-03 (later): R9656 re-transcribed, 61% -> 79%; fraction_read 0.76 (1603/2115 over the five measured letters).

system.summary: Three-letter consonant-vowel-consonant nomenclator codes mixed inline with clear Spanish, with homophones at code level (ta and tu both = 'no'), codes used for syllables as well as whole words, and long words spelled letter by letter between the codes.

system.summary: Three-letter consonant-vowel-consonant nomenclator codes mixed inline with clear Spanish, with homophones at code level (ta and tu both = 'no'), codes used for syllables as well as whole words, and long words spelled letter by letter between the codes.

title: Charles III of Lorraine to the comte de Vaudémont, Nancy, 18 June 1592, BnF fr. 3621 no. 97 (DECODE R9449)
system.summary: Reciprocal letter-pair substitution written in ordinary cursive letterforms (a/i b/p c/f d/q e/t g/u l/y m/z n/s o/r h/x), two dots under a letter for a doubled letter, a null (looped ae), a few special signs, and figures for syllables and words (31 = ma, 139 = vous, 145 = me, 141 = qu'il); λ, γ, U, π, m̄ are nulls.
system.sibling_key: Four 1592 key sheets in the Nevers key book fr. 3995 (ff. 32, 83-84, 98, 103) examined and eliminated; no Lorraine key on DECODE, Cryptiana or in print. None used.
system.notes: Re-read 22 Sept 2026 (ct/no97_reread.txt, ct/no97_reading2.md): the 18 Sept key's values paired reciprocally, and the pair key with the c/e and b/h splits reads the letter. Special signs λ, m̄, U, E, π, γ, ꝗ, figure-4 mostly unresolved.
conditions.prior_solution.where: Tomokiyo, cryptiana unsolved.htm, entry 'Duke of Lorraine (1592)', marked Solved: 'I solved this in 2025', quoting only the opening ("J'ay este infiniment mal satisfait du peu d'execution ...."); no key or text published. Present in the 6 Sept 2026 snapshot (targets/napoleon/unsolved.htm), before the 18 Sept attempt. DECODE R9449 still 'Non-decrypted'; no key anywhere.
conditions.human_role: Outside contribution: the work was done and committed by GitHub user aryasn2026 (git author of all three commits) and merged as pull request #4 after review (docs/lorraine1592.html). What the contributor did beyond running the model is not recorded. The NOTES ask the user to verify the DECODE queries, the Charles II/III identification and every transcription.
conditions.tools: shear deskew and line segmentation (deskew.py); shape clustering (cluster.py, cluster2.py), superseded; homophonic annealer (solve.py), superseded; French 4-gram model from Montaigne (buildlm.py); steepest-ascent iterated local search (search.py, final97.py); word-level refinement (polish97.py); known-key, noise and merge controls (control.py-control4.py); null test (nulltest.py)
outcome.method_basis: The reciprocal letter-pair key recovered from the ciphertext alone (recorded under parts; Tomokiyo had broken it in 2025 without publishing a text) decodes no. 97 into fragments with a gap in almost every line; no sentence of the cipher can be built. Method restored 24 Oct 2026 (George Lasry: a key can be mostly recovered while the text is not read): the key was obtained by recovering the reciprocal letter-pair key from the ciphertext alone; class stays not read, as the text does not read.

title: Otto von der Malsburg to Landgrave Wilhelm V of Hesse-Kassel: ten cipher letters on the war in Westphalia, Jan-Mar 1637 (HStAM 4 h Nr. 1411)
system.summary: The numerical letters use German homophonic substitution and a nomenclator, while the separate ten-line alphabetic block uses repeating shifts 4,5,3,6,2 over abcdefghiklmnopqrstuwxyz with unresolved exceptional code groups.
system.sibling_key: none: 176 HCPortal key records of the Marburg key volumes checked; the Sixtinus key (HCPortal key 5, Dec 1635) has the same layout but a different table
system.notes: Numerical system: 89 two-digit groups, about 20 digraph signs, about 45 codes (151 tokens), a few name signs; numerical assignments are not alphabetically ordered. Alphabetic system: a=0, subtract shifts 4,5,3,6,2 modulo 24 continuously across lines, starting at phase 0. 43, 45 and LL advance zero modulo five in the selected treatment; this establishes neither expansion length nor referent. Annotation [E?]: Sixt: / cla: remains tentative and unexpanded.

This records the contributor stage, not a changed account of the earlier numerical attack.

title: Otto von der Malsburg to Landgrave Wilhelm V of Hesse-Kassel: ten cipher letters on the war in Westphalia, Jan-Mar 1637 (HStAM 4 h Nr. 1411)
system.summary: The numerical letters use German homophonic substitution and a nomenclator, while the separate ten-line alphabetic block uses repeating shifts 4,5,3,6,2 over abcdefghiklmnopqrstuwxyz with unresolved exceptional code groups.
system.sibling_key: none: 176 HCPortal key records of the Marburg key volumes checked; the Sixtinus key (HCPortal key 5, Dec 1635) has the same layout but a different table
system.notes: Numerical system: 89 two-digit groups, about 20 digraph signs, about 45 codes (151 tokens), a few name signs; numerical assignments are not alphabetically ordered. Alphabetic system: a=0, subtract shifts 4,5,3,6,2 modulo 24 continuously across lines, starting at phase 0. 43, 45 and LL advance zero modulo five in the selected treatment; this establishes neither expansion length nor referent. Annotation [E?]: Sixt: / cla: remains tentative and unexpanded.
conditions.prior_solution.where: At the original numerical attempt HCPortal marked all ten records Not solved and no prior edition had been found. Before the separate Beck/ChatGPT alphabetic investigation, Bourdeau had published the numerical decipherment and provisional alphabetic transcription. That surrounding reading was consulted, but no prior decipherment of this alphabetic block or external plaintext crib was established. This records the contributor stage, not a changed account of the earlier numerical attack.

This is an external contribution, not part of the original Claude session; exact contributor model IDs, first-discovery date and session count are unknown.

title: Otto von der Malsburg to Landgrave Wilhelm V of Hesse-Kassel: ten cipher letters on the war in Westphalia, Jan-Mar 1637 (HStAM 4 h Nr. 1411)
system.summary: The numerical letters use German homophonic substitution and a nomenclator, while the separate ten-line alphabetic block uses repeating shifts 4,5,3,6,2 over abcdefghiklmnopqrstuwxyz with unresolved exceptional code groups.
system.sibling_key: none: 176 HCPortal key records of the Marburg key volumes checked; the Sixtinus key (HCPortal key 5, Dec 1635) has the same layout but a different table
system.notes: Numerical system: 89 two-digit groups, about 20 digraph signs, about 45 codes (151 tokens), a few name signs; numerical assignments are not alphabetically ordered. Alphabetic system: a=0, subtract shifts 4,5,3,6,2 modulo 24 continuously across lines, starting at phase 0. 43, 45 and LL advance zero modulo five in the selected treatment; this establishes neither expansion length nor referent. Annotation [E?]: Sixt: / cla: remains tentative and unexpanded.
conditions.prior_solution.where: At the original numerical attempt HCPortal marked all ten records Not solved and no prior edition had been found. Before the separate Beck/ChatGPT alphabetic investigation, Bourdeau had published the numerical decipherment and provisional alphabetic transcription. That surrounding reading was consulted, but no prior decipherment of this alphabetic block or external plaintext crib was established. This records the contributor stage, not a changed account of the earlier numerical attack.

title: Otto von der Malsburg to Landgrave Wilhelm V of Hesse-Kassel: ten cipher letters on the war in Westphalia, Jan-Mar 1637 (HStAM 4 h Nr. 1411)
system.summary: The numerical letters use German homophonic substitution and a nomenclator, while the separate ten-line alphabetic block uses repeating shifts 4,5,3,6,2 over abcdefghiklmnopqrstuwxyz with unresolved exceptional code groups.
system.sibling_key: none: 176 HCPortal key records of the Marburg key volumes checked; the Sixtinus key (HCPortal key 5, Dec 1635) has the same layout but a different table
system.notes: Numerical system: 89 two-digit groups, about 20 digraph signs, about 45 codes (151 tokens), a few name signs; numerical assignments are not alphabetically ordered. Alphabetic system: a=0, subtract shifts 4,5,3,6,2 modulo 24 continuously across lines, starting at phase 0. 43, 45 and LL advance zero modulo five in the selected treatment; this establishes neither expansion length nor referent. Annotation [E?]: Sixt: / cla: remains tentative and unexpanded.
conditions.prior_solution.where: At the original numerical attempt HCPortal marked all ten records Not solved and no prior edition had been found. Before the separate Beck/ChatGPT alphabetic investigation, Bourdeau had published the numerical decipherment and provisional alphabetic transcription. That surrounding reading was consulted, but no prior decipherment of this alphabetic block or external plaintext crib was established. This records the contributor stage, not a changed account of the earlier numerical attack.
