title: Otto von der Malsburg to Landgrave Wilhelm V of Hesse-Kassel: ten cipher letters on the war in Westphalia, Jan-Mar 1637 (HStAM 4 h Nr. 1411)
system.summary: The numerical letters use German homophonic substitution and a nomenclator, while the separate ten-line alphabetic block uses repeating shifts 4,5,3,6,2 over abcdefghiklmnopqrstuwxyz with unresolved exceptional code groups.
system.sibling_key: none: 176 HCPortal key records of the Marburg key volumes checked; the Sixtinus key (HCPortal key 5, Dec 1635) has the same layout but a different table
system.notes: Numerical system: 89 two-digit groups, about 20 digraph signs, about 45 codes (151 tokens), a few name signs; numerical assignments are not alphabetically ordered. Alphabetic system: a=0, subtract shifts 4,5,3,6,2 modulo 24 continuously across lines, starting at phase 0. 43, 45 and LL advance zero modulo five in the selected treatment; this establishes neither expansion length nor referent. Annotation [E?]: Sixt: / cla: remains tentative and unexpanded.
conditions.prior_solution.where: At the original numerical attempt HCPortal marked all ten records Not solved and no prior edition had been found. Before the separate Beck/ChatGPT alphabetic investigation, Bourdeau had published the numerical decipherment and provisional alphabetic transcription. That surrounding reading was consulted, but no prior decipherment of this alphabetic block or external plaintext crib was established. This records the contributor stage, not a changed account of the earlier numerical attack.

title: Otto von der Malsburg to Landgrave Wilhelm V of Hesse-Kassel: ten cipher letters on the war in Westphalia, Jan-Mar 1637 (HStAM 4 h Nr. 1411)
system.summary: The numerical letters use German homophonic substitution and a nomenclator, while the separate ten-line alphabetic block uses repeating shifts 4,5,3,6,2 over abcdefghiklmnopqrstuwxyz with unresolved exceptional code groups.
system.sibling_key: none: 176 HCPortal key records of the Marburg key volumes checked; the Sixtinus key (HCPortal key 5, Dec 1635) has the same layout but a different table
system.notes: Numerical system: 89 two-digit groups, about 20 digraph signs, about 45 codes (151 tokens), a few name signs; numerical assignments are not alphabetically ordered. Alphabetic system: a=0, subtract shifts 4,5,3,6,2 modulo 24 continuously across lines, starting at phase 0. 43, 45 and LL advance zero modulo five in the selected treatment; this establishes neither expansion length nor referent. Annotation [E?]: Sixt: / cla: remains tentative and unexpanded.
conditions.prior_solution.where: At the original numerical attempt HCPortal marked all ten records Not solved and no prior edition had been found. Before the separate Beck/ChatGPT alphabetic investigation, Bourdeau had published the numerical decipherment and provisional alphabetic transcription. That surrounding reading was consulted, but no prior decipherment of this alphabetic block or external plaintext crib was established. This records the contributor stage, not a changed account of the earlier numerical attack.

Later alphabetic contribution: Larry Beck directed a separate ChatGPT investigation, supplied research goals and requested source and computational checks. ChatGPT performed computation, separate image readings and drafting. This is an external contribution, not part of the original Claude session; exact contributor model IDs, first-discovery date and session count are unknown.

outcome.method_basis: Bourdeau recovered the numerical table by ciphertext-only annealing; the separate Beck/ChatGPT contribution recovered the alphabetic repeating shifts from the provisional ciphertext, with subsequent image-reading corrections and no external plaintext crib.

title: Otto von der Malsburg to Landgrave Wilhelm V of Hesse-Kassel: ten cipher letters on the war in Westphalia, Jan-Mar 1637 (HStAM 4 h Nr. 1411)
system.summary: The numerical letters use German homophonic substitution and a nomenclator, while the separate ten-line alphabetic block uses repeating shifts 4,5,3,6,2 over abcdefghiklmnopqrstuwxyz with unresolved exceptional code groups.
system.sibling_key: none: 176 HCPortal key records of the Marburg key volumes checked; the Sixtinus key (HCPortal key 5, Dec 1635) has the same layout but a different table
system.notes: Numerical system: 89 two-digit groups, about 20 digraph signs, about 45 codes (151 tokens), a few name signs; numerical assignments are not alphabetically ordered. Alphabetic system: a=0, subtract shifts 4,5,3,6,2 modulo 24 continuously across lines, starting at phase 0. 43, 45 and LL advance zero modulo five in the selected treatment; this establishes neither expansion length nor referent. Annotation [E?]: Sixt: / cla: remains tentative and unexpanded.

title: Otto von der Malsburg to Landgrave Wilhelm V of Hesse-Kassel: ten cipher letters on the war in Westphalia, Jan-Mar 1637 (HStAM 4 h Nr. 1411)
system.summary: The numerical letters use German homophonic substitution and a nomenclator, while the separate ten-line alphabetic block uses repeating shifts 4,5,3,6,2 over abcdefghiklmnopqrstuwxyz with unresolved exceptional code groups.
system.sibling_key: none: 176 HCPortal key records of the Marburg key volumes checked; the Sixtinus key (HCPortal key 5, Dec 1635) has the same layout but a different table
system.notes: Numerical system: 89 two-digit groups, about 20 digraph signs, about 45 codes (151 tokens), a few name signs; numerical assignments are not alphabetically ordered. Alphabetic system: a=0, subtract shifts 4,5,3,6,2 modulo 24 continuously across lines, starting at phase 0. 43, 45 and LL advance zero modulo five in the selected treatment; this establishes neither expansion length nor referent. Annotation [E?]: Sixt: / cla: remains tentative and unexpanded.
conditions.prior_solution.where: At the original numerical attempt HCPortal marked all ten records Not solved and no prior edition had been found. Before the separate Beck/ChatGPT alphabetic investigation, Bourdeau had published the numerical decipherment and provisional alphabetic transcription. That surrounding reading was consulted, but no prior decipherment of this alphabetic block or external plaintext crib was established. This records the contributor stage, not a changed account of the earlier numerical attack.

ChatGPT performed computation, separate image readings and drafting. This is an external contribution, not part of the original Claude session; exact contributor model IDs, first-discovery date and session count are unknown.

outcome.method_basis: Bourdeau recovered the numerical table by ciphertext-only annealing; the separate Beck/ChatGPT contribution recovered the alphabetic repeating shifts from the provisional ciphertext, with subsequent image-reading corrections and no external plaintext crib.

title: Ferdinand I to Johann Malvezzi, Augsburg, 23 January 1548 (DECODE R366)
system.summary: Monoalphabetic homophonic cipher in graphic signs (alchemical and planetary signs, Greek and Latin letters with other values), two or three signs per common letter, numbers for doubled letters, and a short code list of syllables for the principals.
system.sibling_key: DECODE R367 (same shelfmark) and R386 (NSZL Quart. Lat. 2254. 15)
system.notes: The circle-on-a-stem family of signs is ambiguous between u, e/ae and (with a cross) t; resolved by Latin context. Some signs serve more than one letter in practice. Nomenclator: about 20 code syllables (ki=Rustanus, ka/ke=Passa, le=Charles V, Bi=king of France, Nas/Ras/ye=the Sultan, zes=Queen Isabella, zos=Frater George, Cad=Constantinople, Eb=orator), plus 50=bellum, 51=pax. Nulls are whole Latin-looking words inside the cipher (etiam, idcirco, atque, cum, Porro, Dar, Der, spo, spu) and the loose letters b, d, n, z and a Greek pi.
conditions.prior_solution.where: No decipherment on DECODE or the web. Austro-Turcica 1541-1552 (Munich 1995) prints the Ferdinand-Malvezzi correspondence of early 1548 (Ferdinand's instructions for Malvezzi, 24 Jan 1548, reportedly no. 62; Ferdinand to Justus de Argento, Augsburg 13 Feb 1548, no. 68, pp. 213-15, per Tracy 2021), so this 23 Jan 1548 letter is probably printed there around nos. 62-67 (c. pp. 190-212); number unconfirmed, edition not online, not consulted (checked 2026-09-21).
conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login and passed its session cookie to the model, and set the target with /goal. No target-specific intervention.
conditions.tools: PIL (cropping and zooming the page images)
outcome.method_basis: The key is DECODE R367, a reconstruction filed at the same shelfmark (Military History Archive 1548/3), with a second copy R386; its sign values were calibrated on p. 1 and the cipher runs read from zoomed crops of R366.
outcome.notes: The substance is recovered in full: Ruestem Pasha's standing after the treaty; the French work to break the Habsburg-Ottoman peace because they dare not attack Charles V directly; Malvezzi's pay (2,800 + 1,500 ducats by Justus de Argento, a 3,000-ducat credit repayable at Venice); a master clockmaker to be brought by the secretary; what to answer about the frontier garrisons; and reciprocity for captives freed by the Sultan. Open: a banker's surname, one two-sign group, two lone v signs.

system.summary: Homophonic substitution of graphic signs and figures for French letters, with a numeric nomenclator of common words and names (12 il, 13 qui, 14 que, 35 parce que, 76 le roi de Navarre).
system.doubled_letters: special sign for some (yy = ss, T= = m/mm)
system.sibling_key: Tomokiyo's published partial tables for Mayenne-Forget Cipher-1; used as the starting key and corrected on the leaves.
system.notes: 87 entries in key.json, 42 of them code groups (19 marked unidentified '+', 4 names '*'). Several signs are confusable by shape (i/n/s, s/i, e/u at 0.91-0.93 correlation), so at the level of reading the cipher behaves as polyphonic and the language model chooses. A three-cipher hypothesis was made and retracted: all nine leaves tested answer to Cipher-1. Split on 14 Oct 2026 (one key per entry): Matignon's Cipher-3 leaves (fr. 15572 f. 276, fr. 15571 f. 179) are the entry matignon1586c3. f. 79r, once taken for a crib of 'Cipher-2', is Cipher-1 (the solved key reads it); the genuine Cipher-2 leaves fr. 15572 ff. 218-219 are not part of any entry (not attempted).
conditions.prior_solution.where: Tomokiyo, cryptiana: partial key tables for Cipher-1 and short openings of ff. 143, 150, 154 and 'f. 111'; contemporary decipherments of sibling leaves (f. 14v in f. 15r, f. 18 in f. 19, ff. 78-79 in the margin). Contemporary clear copies of ff. 143, 149v-150 and 154r-v bound as ff. 155-157 of the same volume, overlooked here until Michael Brackx found them (issue #70, 21 Oct 2026). No printed decipherment found (17 Sept 2026).
conditions.inputs: images; published key; cleartext context; crib
conditions.human_role: Project work: no target-specific intervention recorded. From 21 Oct 2026 the entry also carries Michael Brackx's contributed readings and key corrections (issues #64, #68-#71), reviewed and spot-checked here.
conditions.tools: Gallica IIIF fetch (fetch.py); background flattening (flatten.py); line fitting and tiling (fitlines.py, rowcut.py, mtile.py); character 6-gram French LM from Berger de Xivrey (mklm.py); beam decoder over candidate-letter sets (solve.py, dec.py); glyph segmentation and clustering (glyphseg.py, glyphclust.py); exemplar forced alignment (readleaf.py, forcealign.py); annealing solver (hillclimb.py); crib EM aligner (cribem.py)

title: Forget / Mayenne despatches of 1585-86 in Mayenne-Forget Cipher-1, BnF fr. 15572 (+ fr. 15571 f. 177), catalogue item 12
system.summary: Homophonic substitution of graphic signs and figures for French letters, with a numeric nomenclator of common words and names (12 il, 13 qui, 14 que, 35 parce que, 76 le roi de Navarre).
system.doubled_letters: special sign for some (yy = ss, T= = m/mm)
system.sibling_key: Tomokiyo's published partial tables for Mayenne-Forget Cipher-1; used as the starting key and corrected on the leaves.
system.notes: 87 entries in key.json, 42 of them code groups (19 marked unidentified '+', 4 names '*'). Several signs are confusable by shape (i/n/s, s/i, e/u at 0.91-0.93 correlation), so at the level of reading the cipher behaves as polyphonic and the language model chooses. A three-cipher hypothesis was made and retracted: all nine leaves tested answer to Cipher-1. Split on 14 Oct 2026 (one key per entry): Matignon's Cipher-3 leaves (fr. 15572 f. 276, fr. 15571 f. 179) are the entry matignon1586c3. f. 79r, once taken for a crib of 'Cipher-2', is Cipher-1 (the solved key reads it); the genuine Cipher-2 leaves fr. 15572 ff. 218-219 are not part of any entry (not attempted).
conditions.prior_solution.where: Tomokiyo, cryptiana: partial key tables for Cipher-1 and short openings of ff. 143, 150, 154 and 'f. 111'; contemporary decipherments of sibling leaves (f. 14v in f. 15r, f. 18 in f. 19, ff. 78-79 in the margin). Contemporary clear copies of ff. 143, 149v-150 and 154r-v bound as ff. 155-157 of the same volume, overlooked here until Michael Brackx found them (issue #70, 21 Oct 2026). No printed decipherment found (17 Sept 2026).

title: Forget / Mayenne despatches of 1585-86 in Mayenne-Forget Cipher-1, BnF fr. 15572 (+ fr. 15571 f. 177), catalogue item 12
system.summary: Homophonic substitution of graphic signs and figures for French letters, with a numeric nomenclator of common words and names (12 il, 13 qui, 14 que, 35 parce que, 76 le roi de Navarre).
system.doubled_letters: special sign for some (yy = ss, T= = m/mm)
system.sibling_key: Tomokiyo's published partial tables for Mayenne-Forget Cipher-1; used as the starting key and corrected on the leaves.
system.notes: 87 entries in key.json, 42 of them code groups (19 marked unidentified '+', 4 names '*'). Several signs are confusable by shape (i/n/s, s/i, e/u at 0.91-0.93 correlation), so at the level of reading the cipher behaves as polyphonic and the language model chooses. A three-cipher hypothesis was made and retracted: all nine leaves tested answer to Cipher-1. Split on 14 Oct 2026 (one key per entry): Matignon's Cipher-3 leaves (fr. 15572 f. 276, fr. 15571 f. 179) are the entry matignon1586c3. f. 79r, once taken for a crib of 'Cipher-2', is Cipher-1 (the solved key reads it); the genuine Cipher-2 leaves fr. 15572 ff. 218-219 are not part of any entry (not attempted).
conditions.prior_solution.where: Tomokiyo, cryptiana: partial key tables for Cipher-1 and short openings of ff. 143, 150, 154 and 'f. 111'; contemporary decipherments of sibling leaves (f. 14v in f. 15r, f. 18 in f. 19, ff. 78-79 in the margin). Contemporary clear copies of ff. 143, 149v-150 and 154r-v bound as ff. 155-157 of the same volume, overlooked here until Michael Brackx found them (issue #70, 21 Oct 2026). No printed decipherment found (17 Sept 2026).

title: Forget / Mayenne despatches of 1585-86 in Mayenne-Forget Cipher-1, BnF fr. 15572 (+ fr. 15571 f. 177), catalogue item 12
system.summary: Homophonic substitution of graphic signs and figures for French letters, with a numeric nomenclator of common words and names (12 il, 13 qui, 14 que, 35 parce que, 76 le roi de Navarre).
system.doubled_letters: special sign for some (yy = ss, T= = m/mm)
system.sibling_key: Tomokiyo's published partial tables for Mayenne-Forget Cipher-1; used as the starting key and corrected on the leaves.
system.notes: 87 entries in key.json, 42 of them code groups (19 marked unidentified '+', 4 names '*'). Several signs are confusable by shape (i/n/s, s/i, e/u at 0.91-0.93 correlation), so at the level of reading the cipher behaves as polyphonic and the language model chooses. A three-cipher hypothesis was made and retracted: all nine leaves tested answer to Cipher-1. Split on 14 Oct 2026 (one key per entry): Matignon's Cipher-3 leaves (fr. 15572 f. 276, fr. 15571 f. 179) are the entry matignon1586c3. f. 79r, once taken for a crib of 'Cipher-2', is Cipher-1 (the solved key reads it); the genuine Cipher-2 leaves fr. 15572 ff. 218-219 are not part of any entry (not attempted).

Contemporary clear copies of ff. 143, 149v-150 and 154r-v bound as ff. 155-157 of the same volume, overlooked here until Michael Brackx found them (issue #70, 21 Oct 2026). No printed decipherment found (17 Sept 2026).

title: Forget / Mayenne despatches of 1585-86 in Mayenne-Forget Cipher-1, BnF fr. 15572 (+ fr. 15571 f. 177), catalogue item 12
system.summary: Homophonic substitution of graphic signs and figures for French letters, with a numeric nomenclator of common words and names (12 il, 13 qui, 14 que, 35 parce que, 76 le roi de Navarre).
system.doubled_letters: special sign for some (yy = ss, T= = m/mm)
system.sibling_key: Tomokiyo's published partial tables for Mayenne-Forget Cipher-1; used as the starting key and corrected on the leaves.
system.notes: 87 entries in key.json, 42 of them code groups (19 marked unidentified '+', 4 names '*'). Several signs are confusable by shape (i/n/s, s/i, e/u at 0.91-0.93 correlation), so at the level of reading the cipher behaves as polyphonic and the language model chooses. A three-cipher hypothesis was made and retracted: all nine leaves tested answer to Cipher-1. Split on 14 Oct 2026 (one key per entry): Matignon's Cipher-3 leaves (fr. 15572 f. 276, fr. 15571 f. 179) are the entry matignon1586c3. f. 79r, once taken for a crib of 'Cipher-2', is Cipher-1 (the solved key reads it); the genuine Cipher-2 leaves fr. 15572 ff. 218-219 are not part of any entry (not attempted).
conditions.prior_solution.where: Tomokiyo, cryptiana: partial key tables for Cipher-1 and short openings of ff. 143, 150, 154 and 'f. 111'; contemporary decipherments of sibling leaves (f. 14v in f. 15r, f. 18 in f. 19, ff. 78-79 in the margin). Contemporary clear copies of ff. 143, 149v-150 and 154r-v bound as ff. 155-157 of the same volume, overlooked here until Michael Brackx found them (issue #70, 21 Oct 2026). No printed decipherment found (17 Sept 2026).

system.summary: Homophonic substitution of graphic signs and figures for French letters, with a numeric nomenclator of common words and names (12 il, 13 qui, 14 que, 35 parce que, 76 le roi de Navarre).
system.doubled_letters: special sign for some (yy = ss, T= = m/mm)
system.sibling_key: Tomokiyo's published partial tables for Mayenne-Forget Cipher-1; used as the starting key and corrected on the leaves.
system.notes: 87 entries in key.json, 42 of them code groups (19 marked unidentified '+', 4 names '*'). title: Forget / Mayenne despatches of 1585-86 in Mayenne-Forget Cipher-1, BnF fr. 15572 (+ fr. 15571 f. 177), catalogue item 12
system.summary: Homophonic substitution of graphic signs and figures for French letters, with a numeric nomenclator of common words and names (12 il, 13 qui, 14 que, 35 parce que, 76 le roi de Navarre).
system.doubled_letters: special sign for some (yy = ss, T= = m/mm)
system.sibling_key: Tomokiyo's published partial tables for Mayenne-Forget Cipher-1; used as the starting key and corrected on the leaves.
system.notes: 87 entries in key.json, 42 of them code groups (19 marked unidentified '+', 4 names '*'). Several signs are confusable by shape (i/n/s, s/i, e/u at 0.91-0.93 correlation), so at the level of reading the cipher behaves as polyphonic and the language model chooses. A three-cipher hypothesis was made and retracted: all nine leaves tested answer to Cipher-1. Split on 14 Oct 2026 (one key per entry): Matignon's Cipher-3 leaves (fr. 15572 f. 276, fr. 15571 f. 179) are the entry matignon1586c3. f. 79r, once taken for a crib of 'Cipher-2', is Cipher-1 (the solved key reads it); the genuine Cipher-2 leaves fr. 15572 ff. 218-219 are not part of any entry (not attempted).
conditions.prior_solution.where: Tomokiyo, cryptiana: partial key tables for Cipher-1 and short openings of ff. 143, 150, 154 and 'f. 111'; contemporary decipherments of sibling leaves (f. 14v in f. 15r, f. 18 in f. 19, ff. 78-79 in the margin). Contemporary clear copies of ff. 143, 149v-150 and 154r-v bound as ff. 155-157 of the same volume, overlooked here until Michael Brackx found them (issue #70, 21 Oct 2026). No printed decipherment found (17 Sept 2026).

title: Forget / Mayenne despatches of 1585-86 in Mayenne-Forget Cipher-1, BnF fr. 15572 (+ fr. 15571 f. 177), catalogue item 12
system.summary: Homophonic substitution of graphic signs and figures for French letters, with a numeric nomenclator of common words and names (12 il, 13 qui, 14 que, 35 parce que, 76 le roi de Navarre).
system.doubled_letters: special sign for some (yy = ss, T= = m/mm)
system.sibling_key: Tomokiyo's published partial tables for Mayenne-Forget Cipher-1; used as the starting key and corrected on the leaves.
system.notes: 87 entries in key.json, 42 of them code groups (19 marked unidentified '+', 4 names '*'). Several signs are confusable by shape (i/n/s, s/i, e/u at 0.91-0.93 correlation), so at the level of reading the cipher behaves as polyphonic and the language model chooses. A three-cipher hypothesis was made and retracted: all nine leaves tested answer to Cipher-1. Split on 14 Oct 2026 (one key per entry): Matignon's Cipher-3 leaves (fr. 15572 f. 276, fr. 15571 f. 179) are the entry matignon1586c3. f. 79r, once taken for a crib of 'Cipher-2', is Cipher-1 (the solved key reads it); the genuine Cipher-2 leaves fr. 15572 ff. 218-219 are not part of any entry (not attempted).
conditions.prior_solution.where: Tomokiyo, cryptiana: partial key tables for Cipher-1 and short openings of ff. 143, 150, 154 and 'f. 111'; contemporary decipherments of sibling leaves (f. 14v in f. 15r, f. 18 in f. 19, ff. 78-79 in the margin). Contemporary clear copies of ff. 143, 149v-150 and 154r-v bound as ff. 155-157 of the same volume, overlooked here until Michael Brackx found them (issue #70, 21 Oct 2026). No printed decipherment found (17 Sept 2026).

title: Forget / Mayenne despatches of 1585-86 in Mayenne-Forget Cipher-1, BnF fr. 15572 (+ fr. 15571 f. 177), catalogue item 12
system.summary: Homophonic substitution of graphic signs and figures for French letters, with a numeric nomenclator of common words and names (12 il, 13 qui, 14 que, 35 parce que, 76 le roi de Navarre).
system.doubled_letters: special sign for some (yy = ss, T= = m/mm)
system.sibling_key: Tomokiyo's published partial tables for Mayenne-Forget Cipher-1; used as the starting key and corrected on the leaves.
system.notes: 87 entries in key.json, 42 of them code groups (19 marked unidentified '+', 4 names '*'). Several signs are confusable by shape (i/n/s, s/i, e/u at 0.91-0.93 correlation), so at the level of reading the cipher behaves as polyphonic and the language model chooses. A three-cipher hypothesis was made and retracted: all nine leaves tested answer to Cipher-1. Split on 14 Oct 2026 (one key per entry): Matignon's Cipher-3 leaves (fr. 15572 f. 276, fr. 15571 f. 179) are the entry matignon1586c3. f. 79r, once taken for a crib of 'Cipher-2', is Cipher-1 (the solved key reads it); the genuine Cipher-2 leaves fr. 15572 ff. 218-219 are not part of any entry (not attempted).
conditions.prior_solution.where: Tomokiyo, cryptiana: partial key tables for Cipher-1 and short openings of ff. 143, 150, 154 and 'f. 111'; contemporary decipherments of sibling leaves (f. 14v in f. 15r, f. 18 in f. 19, ff. 78-79 in the margin). Contemporary clear copies of ff. 143, 149v-150 and 154r-v bound as ff. 155-157 of the same volume, overlooked here until Michael Brackx found them (issue #70, 21 Oct 2026). No printed decipherment found (17 Sept 2026).

title: Forget / Mayenne despatches of 1585-86 in Mayenne-Forget Cipher-1, BnF fr. 15572 (+ fr. 15571 f. 177), catalogue item 12
system.summary: Homophonic substitution of graphic signs and figures for French letters, with a numeric nomenclator of common words and names (12 il, 13 qui, 14 que, 35 parce que, 76 le roi de Navarre).
system.doubled_letters: special sign for some (yy = ss, T= = m/mm)
system.sibling_key: Tomokiyo's published partial tables for Mayenne-Forget Cipher-1; used as the starting key and corrected on the leaves.
system.notes: 87 entries in key.json, 42 of them code groups (19 marked unidentified '+', 4 names '*'). Several signs are confusable by shape (i/n/s, s/i, e/u at 0.91-0.93 correlation), so at the level of reading the cipher behaves as polyphonic and the language model chooses. A three-cipher hypothesis was made and retracted: all nine leaves tested answer to Cipher-1. Split on 14 Oct 2026 (one key per entry): Matignon's Cipher-3 leaves (fr. 15572 f. 276, fr. 15571 f. 179) are the entry matignon1586c3. f. 79r, once taken for a crib of 'Cipher-2', is Cipher-1 (the solved key reads it); the genuine Cipher-2 leaves fr. 15572 ff. 218-219 are not part of any entry (not attempted).
conditions.prior_solution.where: Tomokiyo, cryptiana: partial key tables for Cipher-1 and short openings of ff. 143, 150, 154 and 'f. 111'; contemporary decipherments of sibling leaves (f. 14v in f. 15r, f. 18 in f. 19, ff. 78-79 in the margin). Contemporary clear copies of ff. 143, 149v-150 and 154r-v bound as ff. 155-157 of the same volume, overlooked here until Michael Brackx found them (issue #70, 21 Oct 2026). No printed decipherment found (17 Sept 2026).

system.summary: Homophonic substitution of graphic signs and figures for French letters, with a numeric nomenclator of common words and names (12 il, 13 qui, 14 que, 35 parce que, 76 le roi de Navarre).
system.doubled_letters: special sign for some (yy = ss, T= = m/mm)
system.sibling_key: Tomokiyo's published partial tables for Mayenne-Forget Cipher-1; used as the starting key and corrected on the leaves.
system.notes: 87 entries in key.json, 42 of them code groups (19 marked unidentified '+', 4 names '*'). Several signs are confusable by shape (i/n/s, s/i, e/u at 0.91-0.93 correlation), so at the level of reading the cipher behaves as polyphonic and the language model chooses. A three-cipher hypothesis was made and retracted: all nine leaves tested answer to Cipher-1. Split on 14 Oct 2026 (one key per entry): Matignon's Cipher-3 leaves (fr. 15572 f. 276, fr. 15571 f. 179) are the entry matignon1586c3. f. 79r, once taken for a crib of 'Cipher-2', is Cipher-1 (the solved key reads it); the genuine Cipher-2 leaves fr. 15572 ff. 218-219 are not part of any entry (not attempted).

Contemporary clear copies of ff. 143, 149v-150 and 154r-v bound as ff. 155-157 of the same volume, overlooked here until Michael Brackx found them (issue #70, 21 Oct 2026). conditions.tools: Gallica IIIF fetch (fetch.py); background flattening (flatten.py); line fitting and tiling (fitlines.py, rowcut.py, mtile.py); character 6-gram French LM from Berger de Xivrey (mklm.py); beam decoder over candidate-letter sets (solve.py, dec.py); glyph segmentation and clustering (glyphseg.py, glyphclust.py); exemplar forced alignment (readleaf.py, forcealign.py); annealing solver (hillclimb.py); crib EM aligner (cribem.py)
outcome.method_basis: Seven leaves read with the Cipher-1 key on the images (Tomokiyo's table, verified on the f. 14/15 and f. 18/19 cribs, merged from Brackx's corrections and extended per leaf), sentence by sentence after George Lasry's review of 22 Oct 2026; four read from contemporary clear copies (ff. 155-157 for ff. 143, 149v-150v, 154; f. 176 for fr. 15571 f. 177), which the key's decode matches.
outcome.contribution: transcription; decipherment with ambiguous key; key extended or corrected
outcome.verification: contemporary decipherment; independent clear copy; matched control; historical consistency
outcome.notes: Measured 22 Sept 2026 with measure.py (rule in its docstring); recalculated 14 Oct 2026 on the Cipher-1 leaves only after the split (Matignon's Cipher-3 leaves are matignon1586c3). title: Forget / Mayenne despatches of 1585-86 in Mayenne-Forget Cipher-1, BnF fr. 15572 (+ fr. 15571 f. 177), catalogue item 12
system.summary: Homophonic substitution of graphic signs and figures for French letters, with a numeric nomenclator of common words and names (12 il, 13 qui, 14 que, 35 parce que, 76 le roi de Navarre).
system.doubled_letters: special sign for some (yy = ss, T= = m/mm)
system.sibling_key: Tomokiyo's published partial tables for Mayenne-Forget Cipher-1; used as the starting key and corrected on the leaves.
system.notes: 87 entries in key.json, 42 of them code groups (19 marked unidentified '+', 4 names '*'). Several signs are confusable by shape (i/n/s, s/i, e/u at 0.91-0.93 correlation), so at the level of reading the cipher behaves as polyphonic and the language model chooses. A three-cipher hypothesis was made and retracted: all nine leaves tested answer to Cipher-1. Split on 14 Oct 2026 (one key per entry): Matignon's Cipher-3 leaves (fr. 15572 f. 276, fr. 15571 f. 179) are the entry matignon1586c3. f. 79r, once taken for a crib of 'Cipher-2', is Cipher-1 (the solved key reads it); the genuine Cipher-2 leaves fr. 15572 ff. 218-219 are not part of any entry (not attempted).

title: Forget / Mayenne despatches of 1585-86 in Mayenne-Forget Cipher-1, BnF fr. 15572 (+ fr. 15571 f. 177), catalogue item 12
system.summary: Homophonic substitution of graphic signs and figures for French letters, with a numeric nomenclator of common words and names (12 il, 13 qui, 14 que, 35 parce que, 76 le roi de Navarre).
system.doubled_letters: special sign for some (yy = ss, T= = m/mm)
system.sibling_key: Tomokiyo's published partial tables for Mayenne-Forget Cipher-1; used as the starting key and corrected on the leaves.
system.notes: 87 entries in key.json, 42 of them code groups (19 marked unidentified '+', 4 names '*'). Several signs are confusable by shape (i/n/s, s/i, e/u at 0.91-0.93 correlation), so at the level of reading the cipher behaves as polyphonic and the language model chooses. A three-cipher hypothesis was made and retracted: all nine leaves tested answer to Cipher-1. Split on 14 Oct 2026 (one key per entry): Matignon's Cipher-3 leaves (fr. 15572 f. 276, fr. 15571 f. 179) are the entry matignon1586c3. f. 79r, once taken for a crib of 'Cipher-2', is Cipher-1 (the solved key reads it); the genuine Cipher-2 leaves fr. 15572 ff. 218-219 are not part of any entry (not attempted).

Contemporary clear copies of ff. 143, 149v-150 and 154r-v bound as ff. 155-157 of the same volume, overlooked here until Michael Brackx found them (issue #70, 21 Oct 2026). title: Forget / Mayenne despatches of 1585-86 in Mayenne-Forget Cipher-1, BnF fr. 15572 (+ fr. 15571 f. 177), catalogue item 12
system.summary: Homophonic substitution of graphic signs and figures for French letters, with a numeric nomenclator of common words and names (12 il, 13 qui, 14 que, 35 parce que, 76 le roi de Navarre).
system.doubled_letters: special sign for some (yy = ss, T= = m/mm)
system.sibling_key: Tomokiyo's published partial tables for Mayenne-Forget Cipher-1; used as the starting key and corrected on the leaves.
system.notes: 87 entries in key.json, 42 of them code groups (19 marked unidentified '+', 4 names '*'). Several signs are confusable by shape (i/n/s, s/i, e/u at 0.91-0.93 correlation), so at the level of reading the cipher behaves as polyphonic and the language model chooses. A three-cipher hypothesis was made and retracted: all nine leaves tested answer to Cipher-1. Split on 14 Oct 2026 (one key per entry): Matignon's Cipher-3 leaves (fr. 15572 f. 276, fr. 15571 f. 179) are the entry matignon1586c3. f. 79r, once taken for a crib of 'Cipher-2', is Cipher-1 (the solved key reads it); the genuine Cipher-2 leaves fr. 15572 ff. 218-219 are not part of any entry (not attempted).
conditions.prior_solution.where: Tomokiyo, cryptiana: partial key tables for Cipher-1 and short openings of ff. 143, 150, 154 and 'f. 111'; contemporary decipherments of sibling leaves (f. 14v in f. 15r, f. 18 in f. 19, ff. 78-79 in the margin). Contemporary clear copies of ff. 143, 149v-150 and 154r-v bound as ff. 155-157 of the same volume, overlooked here until Michael Brackx found them (issue #70, 21 Oct 2026). No printed decipherment found (17 Sept 2026).

title: Forget / Mayenne despatches of 1585-86 in Mayenne-Forget Cipher-1, BnF fr. 15572 (+ fr. 15571 f. 177), catalogue item 12
system.summary: Homophonic substitution of graphic signs and figures for French letters, with a numeric nomenclator of common words and names (12 il, 13 qui, 14 que, 35 parce que, 76 le roi de Navarre).
system.doubled_letters: special sign for some (yy = ss, T= = m/mm)
system.sibling_key: Tomokiyo's published partial tables for Mayenne-Forget Cipher-1; used as the starting key and corrected on the leaves.
system.notes: 87 entries in key.json, 42 of them code groups (19 marked unidentified '+', 4 names '*'). Several signs are confusable by shape (i/n/s, s/i, e/u at 0.91-0.93 correlation), so at the level of reading the cipher behaves as polyphonic and the language model chooses. A three-cipher hypothesis was made and retracted: all nine leaves tested answer to Cipher-1. Split on 14 Oct 2026 (one key per entry): Matignon's Cipher-3 leaves (fr. 15572 f. 276, fr. 15571 f. 179) are the entry matignon1586c3. f. 79r, once taken for a crib of 'Cipher-2', is Cipher-1 (the solved key reads it); the genuine Cipher-2 leaves fr. 15572 ff. 218-219 are not part of any entry (not attempted).
conditions.prior_solution.where: Tomokiyo, cryptiana: partial key tables for Cipher-1 and short openings of ff. 143, 150, 154 and 'f. 111'; contemporary decipherments of sibling leaves (f. 14v in f. 15r, f. 18 in f. 19, ff. 78-79 in the margin). Contemporary clear copies of ff. 143, 149v-150 and 154r-v bound as ff. 155-157 of the same volume, overlooked here until Michael Brackx found them (issue #70, 21 Oct 2026). No printed decipherment found (17 Sept 2026).

title: Forget / Mayenne despatches of 1585-86 in Mayenne-Forget Cipher-1, BnF fr. 15572 (+ fr. 15571 f. 177), catalogue item 12
system.summary: Homophonic substitution of graphic signs and figures for French letters, with a numeric nomenclator of common words and names (12 il, 13 qui, 14 que, 35 parce que, 76 le roi de Navarre).
system.doubled_letters: special sign for some (yy = ss, T= = m/mm)
system.sibling_key: Tomokiyo's published partial tables for Mayenne-Forget Cipher-1; used as the starting key and corrected on the leaves.
system.notes: 87 entries in key.json, 42 of them code groups (19 marked unidentified '+', 4 names '*'). Several signs are confusable by shape (i/n/s, s/i, e/u at 0.91-0.93 correlation), so at the level of reading the cipher behaves as polyphonic and the language model chooses. A three-cipher hypothesis was made and retracted: all nine leaves tested answer to Cipher-1. Split on 14 Oct 2026 (one key per entry): Matignon's Cipher-3 leaves (fr. 15572 f. 276, fr. 15571 f. 179) are the entry matignon1586c3. f. 79r, once taken for a crib of 'Cipher-2', is Cipher-1 (the solved key reads it); the genuine Cipher-2 leaves fr. 15572 ff. 218-219 are not part of any entry (not attempted).
conditions.prior_solution.where: Tomokiyo, cryptiana: partial key tables for Cipher-1 and short openings of ff. 143, 150, 154 and 'f. 111'; contemporary decipherments of sibling leaves (f. 14v in f. 15r, f. 18 in f. 19, ff. 78-79 in the margin). Contemporary clear copies of ff. 143, 149v-150 and 154r-v bound as ff. 155-157 of the same volume, overlooked here until Michael Brackx found them (issue #70, 21 Oct 2026). No printed decipherment found (17 Sept 2026).

title: Mémoire en chiffre du XIIe décembre 1560: anonymous report from the Agenais to Montmorency, BnF fr. 3157 no. 67
system.summary: Homophonic substitution in a cursive pseudo-script with word division, two-stroke units (zo=u, pp=m, s3=r, lz=d) and four whole-word codes (pour, roy, et, sieur).
system.sibling_key: none
system.notes: Main trap: the rounder r-form (n) versus x (e). Polyphonic delta (u/v, b, g) and double dagger (i, a). No name codes; all persons and places spelt out.
conditions.prior_solution.where: G. Lasry solved it independently in 2023 (improved Feb 2026), unpublished (private communication, 25 Sept 2026). No DECODE record, not on Tomokiyo or Lasry (GL.htm) lists, no edition found by web search. Brunet 2019 on Clairac not reachable.
conditions.human_role: Project-level: posed the catalogue entry with /goal. No target-specific intervention.

title: Frederick II to Louis Michell (London), Berlin 28 Dec 1751, KHA Prins Willem V inv. 198 (DECODE R1957), in the King's cabinet code
system.summary: Frederick II's cabinet code of 1751 to Michell: a numerical nomenclator, point-separated groups 2-6472, with homophones for common words, separate groups for endings and phrase groups.
system.sibling_key: The same cabinet code is used in six King-to-Michell letters of Nov-Dec 1751 in Nationaal Archief 1.10.29 (Fagel) inv. 5177, whose printed concepts (PC 8) gave WAINUT the key (11 Oct 2026). The ministerial letter of the same day (DECODE R1955) is in a different code, Michell's envoy code, and is a separate entry (targets/r1955/).

The ms separates groups with points; the transcription files use spaces. WAINUT key reconstruction (11 Oct 2026, key1751/key_cabinet_v2_final.tsv) confirms 1064, 545, 4364, 87, gives 4310 as the phrase group 'le roi de Sardaigne', and differs on 3042 (sur; dessein = 700), 169 (que), 47 (probably affaire), 1555 1550 (opening pair; et suis = 15 144); 1900 = Pologne, 4366 = le. title: Duplessis-Mornay correspondents 1593-1597: undeciphered figures printed in the 1824 Mémoires et correspondance
system.summary: Numeric groups of 2-4 digits separated by full stops, set inside clear letters. Most groups split into two numbers of 2-24 (2210 = 22|10, 912 = 9|12); the editors of 1824 printed them as figures because they had no key.
system.notes: Same system in both writers' letters (shared groups 199, 515, 129, 814, 1220), so it is probably Duplessis's cipher with his Paris correspondents in 1593.

title: Cardinal Morosini, nuncio and legate in France, to Rome, 1587-89: 35 cipher enclosures in Meister's key no. 40 (AAV Segr. Stato Francia 22, DECODE R18-R22, R27-R49, R51, R52, R55-R58; Francia 18/3, DECODE R17)
system.summary: Meister no. 40 (1587): homophonic letters, clusters and common words in 1-3 digit figures run together without separators, three-digit dotted nomenclator, nulls 8x.
system.sibling_key: none used (R53/R54 of the same volume are in a second key, F22b: targets/morosini1589)
system.notes: Decoded by beam search over segmentations scored with the shared it-cinquecento 5-gram model (decrypt.py). Null rule: 8 plus any following digit.
conditions.prior_solution.where: Key printed in Meister, Die Geheimschrift im Dienste der paepstlichen Kurie (1906) no. 40; Lasry's partial reconstruction on DECODE R18 (DOC_3175, Oct 2020) with the note 'full key in Meister'; no plaintext posted, records listed 'partially decrypted'. R17's DECODE note names the same Meister key; its decryption file is a Java error trace. Found 22 Oct 2026, after the readings: Rome deciphered these letters at the time (ASV Segr. Stato Francia 27, cited by Hübner 1870, not imaged), and Tempesti 1754 paraphrases parts of many of them.
conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login and passed its session cookie to the model, set up Claude Code and posed the problem; no target-specific intervention recorded.
conditions.tools: decrypt.py (beam-search segmentation); lang/ it-cinquecento model
outcome.method_basis: Meister 1906 no. 40, the key printed for Morosini's nunciature (Lasry's partial reconstruction on DECODE R18), applied to DECODE's volunteer transcriptions. The character decode left garbled words in most lines; on 22 Oct 2026 a word-level decoder with a transcription-slip model and a hand re-parse of every break on the figures (and on the images where a figure was in doubt) turned 34 of the 35 enclosures into sentences, translated; most garbles were spurious nomenclator dots in the transcriptions and the clerk's -mente abbreviation (m + null 8). R35, a Spanish copy, still has too many holes.
outcome.contribution: decipherment with ambiguous key; transcription; catalogue correction; sender or date identified
outcome.notes: Split 14 Oct 2026 (one key per entry): the two F22b enclosures R53/R54 are now morosini1589; R17 (Francia 18/3, read 21 Sept 2026 in bergamo1585) moved here, same key. Measured 14 Oct 2026: 0.998 of units have a value over the 35 records; codes_open counts the five R17 codes (the off-list dotted codes of Francia 22 are thought to be transcription slips, not counted). 22 Oct 2026, reading audit: all 35 decoded, not read (class not read). Same day re-read (batch b00): 34 read as sentences and translated, R35 not yet; class read in part. The dotted codes outside Meister's list (162, 191, 250, 516, 617, 716, 770 ...) turned out to be spurious dots on letter groups or real codes with the dot on the wrong figure; no new code value. Abbreviations: m + 8 = -mente, 8 also after other short forms (bo. mem., S. Alt.).

conditions.prior_solution.where: Key printed in Meister, Die Geheimschrift im Dienste der paepstlichen Kurie (1906) no. 40; Lasry's partial reconstruction on DECODE R18 (DOC_3175, Oct 2020) with the note 'full key in Meister'; no plaintext posted, records listed 'partially decrypted'. R17's DECODE note names the same Meister key; its decryption file is a Java error trace. Found 22 Oct 2026, after the readings: Rome deciphered these letters at the time (ASV Segr. Stato Francia 27, cited by Hübner 1870, not imaged), and Tempesti 1754 paraphrases parts of many of them.

outcome.method_basis: Meister 1906 no. 40, the key printed for Morosini's nunciature (Lasry's partial reconstruction on DECODE R18), applied to DECODE's volunteer transcriptions. The character decode left garbled words in most lines; on 22 Oct 2026 a word-level decoder with a transcription-slip model and a hand re-parse of every break on the figures (and on the images where a figure was in doubt) turned 34 of the 35 enclosures into sentences, translated; most garbles were spurious nomenclator dots in the transcriptions and the clerk's -mente abbreviation (m + null 8). R35, a Spanish copy, still has too many holes.

outcome.notes: Split 14 Oct 2026 (one key per entry): the two F22b enclosures R53/R54 are now morosini1589; R17 (Francia 18/3, read 21 Sept 2026 in bergamo1585) moved here, same key. Measured 14 Oct 2026: 0.998 of units have a value over the 35 records; codes_open counts the five R17 codes (the off-list dotted codes of Francia 22 are thought to be transcription slips, not counted). 22 Oct 2026, reading audit: all 35 decoded, not read (class not read). Same day re-read (batch b00): 34 read as sentences and translated, R35 not yet; class read in part. The dotted codes outside Meister's list (162, 191, 250, 516, 617, 716, 770 ...) turned out to be spurious dots on letter groups or real codes with the dot on the wrong figure; no new code value. Abbreviations: m + 8 = -mente, 8 also after other short forms (bo. mem., S. Alt.).

outcome.method_basis: George Lasry's 2020 reconstructed key was attached to every DECODE record R85-R90 before the attempt; it is polyphonic (each digit two letters, zero a null). The beam search under it gave fragments only. On 22 Oct 2026 the contemporary decipherment of R87 (f. 251r, a DECODE cleartext image) was transcribed and aligned with the figures, and the three cipher copies of the 4 Nov 1567 letter (R88, R89, R90, with the clear sentence on f. 302r) were read against each other; they fixed the code values (8010 Regina [di Francia], 4010 S.M., 1020 essere, 1040 lettera, 8030 religione, 8070 ugonotta, 8080 heretici, 8090 havere), with which all six were read word by word on the figures, twelve transcription labels corrected on the images.

Serrano 1914 not reached (HathiTrust 403, not on archive.org).

title: Segreteria di Stato (Rome) to the Nuncio in Spain, 24 ciphered despatches, 4 Jan 1718 - 6 Jan 1720, ASV Segr. Stato Spagna 364D (DECODE R154-R177)
system.summary: Undivided digit stream: two-digit homophones for letters and a few syllables, four-digit nomenclator groups prefixed 4, and the single digit 3 as a null.
system.sibling_key: None needed: the same key serves Spagna 364C (items 1-32) and 364D (items 1-24), 1717-1720.
system.notes: Nomenclator runs: 4001-4078 particles and endings; 4079-4296 nouns and names A-R; 4401-4479 S-V; 4485-4531 calendar and day numbers; 4532-4543 and 4552-4563 two parallel Gennaio-Dicembre month runs; 4535-4619 a second alphabetical run A-T; scattered blocks at 4681, 4706, 4870+. Lasry's filed key gives 268 of the 399 four-digit groups used in the corpus; 61 more were recovered in this session, leaving 135 distinct groups (3.4% of nomenclator tokens) without a value. The digit 3 is a null, except when it falls among the three digits following a 4 prefix, where it belongs to the nomenclator group.

title: Segreteria di Stato (Rome) to the Nuncio in Spain, 24 ciphered despatches, 4 Jan 1718 - 6 Jan 1720, ASV Segr. Stato Spagna 364D (DECODE R154-R177)
system.summary: Undivided digit stream: two-digit homophones for letters and a few syllables, four-digit nomenclator groups prefixed 4, and the single digit 3 as a null.
system.sibling_key: None needed: the same key serves Spagna 364C (items 1-32) and 364D (items 1-24), 1717-1720.
system.notes: Nomenclator runs: 4001-4078 particles and endings; 4079-4296 nouns and names A-R; 4401-4479 S-V; 4485-4531 calendar and day numbers; 4532-4543 and 4552-4563 two parallel Gennaio-Dicembre month runs; 4535-4619 a second alphabetical run A-T; scattered blocks at 4681, 4706, 4870+. Lasry's filed key gives 268 of the 399 four-digit groups used in the corpus; 61 more were recovered in this session, leaving 135 distinct groups (3.4% of nomenclator tokens) without a value. The digit 3 is a null, except when it falls among the three digits following a 4 prefix, where it belongs to the nomenclator group.

outcome.method_basis: Lasry's reconstructed S364 key (24 Oct 2020) and his segmented decipherment of the whole corpus were attached to every DECODE record R154-R177 before the attempt; the project measured that reading and recovered 61 more nomenclator groups from alphabetical brackets and context.
outcome.contribution: key extended or corrected; catalogue correction
outcome.verification: key confirms; contemporary decipherment; historical consistency
outcome.notes: Solved by George Lasry in October 2020 and already read on the DECODE records when this session began; nothing about the system was open. What is new here is the measurement of that reading and 61 additional nomenclator values that extend his key. Verification detail: coverage measured token by token off Lasry's aligned decipherment; each recovered group rests on two or more independent contexts and usually the alphabetical bracket; 4538=Luglio matches the known date of Alberoni's promotion, 12 July 1717. 22 Oct 2026, reading audit: R154 and R173 decoded, not read; R166, R168, R170 overturned to B; fraction_read 0.9789 -> 0.889. Class already solved kept (Lasry's decryption, 2020). 23 Oct 2026, re-read (b22): R154 and R173 read from the complete contemporary interlinear decipherments on the DECODE images, aligned with the figures; six key values corrected or added (key_b22.tsv); all 24 despatches read.

title: Segreteria di Stato (Rome) to the Nuncio in Spain, 24 ciphered despatches, 4 Jan 1718 - 6 Jan 1720, ASV Segr. Stato Spagna 364D (DECODE R154-R177)
system.summary: Undivided digit stream: two-digit homophones for letters and a few syllables, four-digit nomenclator groups prefixed 4, and the single digit 3 as a null.
system.sibling_key: None needed: the same key serves Spagna 364C (items 1-32) and 364D (items 1-24), 1717-1720.
system.notes: Nomenclator runs: 4001-4078 particles and endings; 4079-4296 nouns and names A-R; 4401-4479 S-V; 4485-4531 calendar and day numbers; 4532-4543 and 4552-4563 two parallel Gennaio-Dicembre month runs; 4535-4619 a second alphabetical run A-T; scattered blocks at 4681, 4706, 4870+. Lasry's filed key gives 268 of the 399 four-digit groups used in the corpus; 61 more were recovered in this session, leaving 135 distinct groups (3.4% of nomenclator tokens) without a value. The digit 3 is a null, except when it falls among the three digits following a 4 prefix, where it belongs to the nomenclator group.

outcome.method_basis: Lasry's reconstructed S364 key (24 Oct 2020) and his segmented decipherment of the whole corpus were attached to every DECODE record R154-R177 before the attempt; the project measured that reading and recovered 61 more nomenclator groups from alphabetical brackets and context.

outcome.notes: Solved by George Lasry in October 2020 and already read on the DECODE records when this session began; nothing about the system was open. What is new here is the measurement of that reading and 61 additional nomenclator values that extend his key. Verification detail: coverage measured token by token off Lasry's aligned decipherment; each recovered group rests on two or more independent contexts and usually the alphabetical bracket; 4538=Luglio matches the known date of Alberoni's promotion, 12 July 1717. 22 Oct 2026, reading audit: R154 and R173 decoded, not read; R166, R168, R170 overturned to B; fraction_read 0.9789 -> 0.889. Class already solved kept (Lasry's decryption, 2020). 23 Oct 2026, re-read (b22): R154 and R173 read from the complete contemporary interlinear decipherments on the DECODE images, aligned with the figures; six key values corrected or added (key_b22.tsv); all 24 despatches read.

title: Segreteria di Stato (Rome) to the Nuncio in Spain, 24 ciphered despatches, 4 Jan 1718 - 6 Jan 1720, ASV Segr. Stato Spagna 364D (DECODE R154-R177)
system.summary: Undivided digit stream: two-digit homophones for letters and a few syllables, four-digit nomenclator groups prefixed 4, and the single digit 3 as a null.
system.sibling_key: None needed: the same key serves Spagna 364C (items 1-32) and 364D (items 1-24), 1717-1720.
system.notes: Nomenclator runs: 4001-4078 particles and endings; 4079-4296 nouns and names A-R; 4401-4479 S-V; 4485-4531 calendar and day numbers; 4532-4543 and 4552-4563 two parallel Gennaio-Dicembre month runs; 4535-4619 a second alphabetical run A-T; scattered blocks at 4681, 4706, 4870+. Lasry's filed key gives 268 of the 399 four-digit groups used in the corpus; 61 more were recovered in this session, leaving 135 distinct groups (3.4% of nomenclator tokens) without a value. The digit 3 is a null, except when it falls among the three digits following a 4 prefix, where it belongs to the nomenclator group.

outcome.method_basis: Lasry's reconstructed S364 key (24 Oct 2020) and his segmented decipherment of the whole corpus were attached to every DECODE record R154-R177 before the attempt; the project measured that reading and recovered 61 more nomenclator groups from alphabetical brackets and context.

outcome.notes: Solved by George Lasry in October 2020 and already read on the DECODE records when this session began; nothing about the system was open. What is new here is the measurement of that reading and 61 additional nomenclator values that extend his key. Verification detail: coverage measured token by token off Lasry's aligned decipherment; each recovered group rests on two or more independent contexts and usually the alphabetical bracket; 4538=Luglio matches the known date of Alberoni's promotion, 12 July 1717. 22 Oct 2026, reading audit: R154 and R173 decoded, not read; R166, R168, R170 overturned to B; fraction_read 0.9789 -> 0.889. Class already solved kept (Lasry's decryption, 2020). 23 Oct 2026, re-read (b22): R154 and R173 read from the complete contemporary interlinear decipherments on the DECODE images, aligned with the figures; six key values corrected or added (key_b22.tsv); all 24 despatches read.

title: Segreteria di Stato (Rome) to the Nuncio in Spain, 24 ciphered despatches, 4 Jan 1718 - 6 Jan 1720, ASV Segr. Stato Spagna 364D (DECODE R154-R177)
system.summary: Undivided digit stream: two-digit homophones for letters and a few syllables, four-digit nomenclator groups prefixed 4, and the single digit 3 as a null.
system.sibling_key: None needed: the same key serves Spagna 364C (items 1-32) and 364D (items 1-24), 1717-1720.
system.notes: Nomenclator runs: 4001-4078 particles and endings; 4079-4296 nouns and names A-R; 4401-4479 S-V; 4485-4531 calendar and day numbers; 4532-4543 and 4552-4563 two parallel Gennaio-Dicembre month runs; 4535-4619 a second alphabetical run A-T; scattered blocks at 4681, 4706, 4870+. Lasry's filed key gives 268 of the 399 four-digit groups used in the corpus; 61 more were recovered in this session, leaving 135 distinct groups (3.4% of nomenclator tokens) without a value. The digit 3 is a null, except when it falls among the three digits following a 4 prefix, where it belongs to the nomenclator group.

outcome.notes: Solved by George Lasry in October 2020 and already read on the DECODE records when this session began; nothing about the system was open. What is new here is the measurement of that reading and 61 additional nomenclator values that extend his key. Verification detail: coverage measured token by token off Lasry's aligned decipherment; each recovered group rests on two or more independent contexts and usually the alphabetical bracket; 4538=Luglio matches the known date of Alberoni's promotion, 12 July 1717. 22 Oct 2026, reading audit: R154 and R173 decoded, not read; R166, R168, R170 overturned to B; fraction_read 0.9789 -> 0.889. title: Segreteria di Stato (Rome) to the Nuncio in Spain, 24 ciphered despatches, 4 Jan 1718 - 6 Jan 1720, ASV Segr. Stato Spagna 364D (DECODE R154-R177)
system.summary: Undivided digit stream: two-digit homophones for letters and a few syllables, four-digit nomenclator groups prefixed 4, and the single digit 3 as a null.
system.sibling_key: None needed: the same key serves Spagna 364C (items 1-32) and 364D (items 1-24), 1717-1720.
system.notes: Nomenclator runs: 4001-4078 particles and endings; 4079-4296 nouns and names A-R; 4401-4479 S-V; 4485-4531 calendar and day numbers; 4532-4543 and 4552-4563 two parallel Gennaio-Dicembre month runs; 4535-4619 a second alphabetical run A-T; scattered blocks at 4681, 4706, 4870+. Lasry's filed key gives 268 of the 399 four-digit groups used in the corpus; 61 more were recovered in this session, leaving 135 distinct groups (3.4% of nomenclator tokens) without a value. The digit 3 is a null, except when it falls among the three digits following a 4 prefix, where it belongs to the nomenclator group.

outcome.method_basis: Lasry's reconstructed S364 key (24 Oct 2020) and his segmented decipherment of the whole corpus were attached to every DECODE record R154-R177 before the attempt; the project measured that reading and recovered 61 more nomenclator groups from alphabetical brackets and context.

outcome.notes: Solved by George Lasry in October 2020 and already read on the DECODE records when this session began; nothing about the system was open. What is new here is the measurement of that reading and 61 additional nomenclator values that extend his key. Verification detail: coverage measured token by token off Lasry's aligned decipherment; each recovered group rests on two or more independent contexts and usually the alphabetical bracket; 4538=Luglio matches the known date of Alberoni's promotion, 12 July 1717. 22 Oct 2026, reading audit: R154 and R173 decoded, not read; R166, R168, R170 overturned to B; fraction_read 0.9789 -> 0.889. Class already solved kept (Lasry's decryption, 2020). 23 Oct 2026, re-read (b22): R154 and R173 read from the complete contemporary interlinear decipherments on the DECODE images, aligned with the figures; six key values corrected or added (key_b22.tsv); all 24 despatches read.

title: Segreteria di Stato (Rome) to the Nuncio in Spain, 24 ciphered despatches, 4 Jan 1718 - 6 Jan 1720, ASV Segr. Stato Spagna 364D (DECODE R154-R177)
system.summary: Undivided digit stream: two-digit homophones for letters and a few syllables, four-digit nomenclator groups prefixed 4, and the single digit 3 as a null.
system.sibling_key: None needed: the same key serves Spagna 364C (items 1-32) and 364D (items 1-24), 1717-1720.
system.notes: Nomenclator runs: 4001-4078 particles and endings; 4079-4296 nouns and names A-R; 4401-4479 S-V; 4485-4531 calendar and day numbers; 4532-4543 and 4552-4563 two parallel Gennaio-Dicembre month runs; 4535-4619 a second alphabetical run A-T; scattered blocks at 4681, 4706, 4870+. Lasry's filed key gives 268 of the 399 four-digit groups used in the corpus; 61 more were recovered in this session, leaving 135 distinct groups (3.4% of nomenclator tokens) without a value. The digit 3 is a null, except when it falls among the three digits following a 4 prefix, where it belongs to the nomenclator group.

outcome.notes: Solved by George Lasry in October 2020 and already read on the DECODE records when this session began; nothing about the system was open. What is new here is the measurement of that reading and 61 additional nomenclator values that extend his key. Verification detail: coverage measured token by token off Lasry's aligned decipherment; each recovered group rests on two or more independent contexts and usually the alphabetical bracket; 4538=Luglio matches the known date of Alberoni's promotion, 12 July 1717. 22 Oct 2026, reading audit: R154 and R173 decoded, not read; R166, R168, R170 overturned to B; fraction_read 0.9789 -> 0.889. Class already solved kept (Lasry's decryption, 2020). 23 Oct 2026, re-read (b22): R154 and R173 read from the complete contemporary interlinear decipherments on the DECODE images, aligned with the figures; six key values corrected or added (key_b22.tsv); all 24 despatches read.

title: Segreteria di Stato (Rome) to the Nuncio in Spain, 24 ciphered despatches, 4 Jan 1718 - 6 Jan 1720, ASV Segr. Stato Spagna 364D (DECODE R154-R177)
system.summary: Undivided digit stream: two-digit homophones for letters and a few syllables, four-digit nomenclator groups prefixed 4, and the single digit 3 as a null.
system.sibling_key: None needed: the same key serves Spagna 364C (items 1-32) and 364D (items 1-24), 1717-1720.
system.notes: Nomenclator runs: 4001-4078 particles and endings; 4079-4296 nouns and names A-R; 4401-4479 S-V; 4485-4531 calendar and day numbers; 4532-4543 and 4552-4563 two parallel Gennaio-Dicembre month runs; 4535-4619 a second alphabetical run A-T; scattered blocks at 4681, 4706, 4870+. Lasry's filed key gives 268 of the 399 four-digit groups used in the corpus; 61 more were recovered in this session, leaving 135 distinct groups (3.4% of nomenclator tokens) without a value. The digit 3 is a null, except when it falls among the three digits following a 4 prefix, where it belongs to the nomenclator group.

outcome.method_basis: Lasry's reconstructed S364 key (24 Oct 2020) and his segmented decipherment of the whole corpus were attached to every DECODE record R154-R177 before the attempt; the project measured that reading and recovered 61 more nomenclator groups from alphabetical brackets and context.

outcome.verification: key confirms; contemporary decipherment; historical consistency
outcome.notes: Solved by George Lasry in October 2020 and already read on the DECODE records when this session began; nothing about the system was open. What is new here is the measurement of that reading and 61 additional nomenclator values that extend his key. Verification detail: coverage measured token by token off Lasry's aligned decipherment; each recovered group rests on two or more independent contexts and usually the alphabetical bracket; 4538=Luglio matches the known date of Alberoni's promotion, 12 July 1717. 22 Oct 2026, reading audit: R154 and R173 decoded, not read; R166, R168, R170 overturned to B; fraction_read 0.9789 -> 0.889. Class already solved kept (Lasry's decryption, 2020). 23 Oct 2026, re-read (b22): R154 and R173 read from the complete contemporary interlinear decipherments on the DECODE images, aligned with the figures; six key values corrected or added (key_b22.tsv); all 24 despatches read.

title: Segreteria di Stato (Rome) to the Nuncio in Spain, 24 ciphered despatches, 4 Jan 1718 - 6 Jan 1720, ASV Segr. Stato Spagna 364D (DECODE R154-R177)
system.summary: Undivided digit stream: two-digit homophones for letters and a few syllables, four-digit nomenclator groups prefixed 4, and the single digit 3 as a null.
system.sibling_key: None needed: the same key serves Spagna 364C (items 1-32) and 364D (items 1-24), 1717-1720.
system.notes: Nomenclator runs: 4001-4078 particles and endings; 4079-4296 nouns and names A-R; 4401-4479 S-V; 4485-4531 calendar and day numbers; 4532-4543 and 4552-4563 two parallel Gennaio-Dicembre month runs; 4535-4619 a second alphabetical run A-T; scattered blocks at 4681, 4706, 4870+. Lasry's filed key gives 268 of the 399 four-digit groups used in the corpus; 61 more were recovered in this session, leaving 135 distinct groups (3.4% of nomenclator tokens) without a value. The digit 3 is a null, except when it falls among the three digits following a 4 prefix, where it belongs to the nomenclator group.

outcome.method_basis: Lasry's reconstructed S364 key (24 Oct 2020) and his segmented decipherment of the whole corpus were attached to every DECODE record R154-R177 before the attempt; the project measured that reading and recovered 61 more nomenclator groups from alphabetical brackets and context.

outcome.notes: Solved by George Lasry in October 2020 and already read on the DECODE records when this session began; nothing about the system was open. What is new here is the measurement of that reading and 61 additional nomenclator values that extend his key. Verification detail: coverage measured token by token off Lasry's aligned decipherment; each recovered group rests on two or more independent contexts and usually the alphabetical bracket; 4538=Luglio matches the known date of Alberoni's promotion, 12 July 1717. 22 Oct 2026, reading audit: R154 and R173 decoded, not read; R166, R168, R170 overturned to B; fraction_read 0.9789 -> 0.889. Class already solved kept (Lasry's decryption, 2020). 23 Oct 2026, re-read (b22): R154 and R173 read from the complete contemporary interlinear decipherments on the DECODE images, aligned with the figures; six key values corrected or added (key_b22.tsv); all 24 despatches read.

title: Segreteria di Stato (Rome) to the Nuncio in Spain, 24 ciphered despatches, 4 Jan 1718 - 6 Jan 1720, ASV Segr. Stato Spagna 364D (DECODE R154-R177)
system.summary: Undivided digit stream: two-digit homophones for letters and a few syllables, four-digit nomenclator groups prefixed 4, and the single digit 3 as a null.
system.sibling_key: None needed: the same key serves Spagna 364C (items 1-32) and 364D (items 1-24), 1717-1720.
system.notes: Nomenclator runs: 4001-4078 particles and endings; 4079-4296 nouns and names A-R; 4401-4479 S-V; 4485-4531 calendar and day numbers; 4532-4543 and 4552-4563 two parallel Gennaio-Dicembre month runs; 4535-4619 a second alphabetical run A-T; scattered blocks at 4681, 4706, 4870+. Lasry's filed key gives 268 of the 399 four-digit groups used in the corpus; 61 more were recovered in this session, leaving 135 distinct groups (3.4% of nomenclator tokens) without a value. The digit 3 is a null, except when it falls among the three digits following a 4 prefix, where it belongs to the nomenclator group.

outcome.notes: Solved by George Lasry in October 2020 and already read on the DECODE records when this session began; nothing about the system was open. What is new here is the measurement of that reading and 61 additional nomenclator values that extend his key. Verification detail: coverage measured token by token off Lasry's aligned decipherment; each recovered group rests on two or more independent contexts and usually the alphabetical bracket; 4538=Luglio matches the known date of Alberoni's promotion, 12 July 1717. 22 Oct 2026, reading audit: R154 and R173 decoded, not read; R166, R168, R170 overturned to B; fraction_read 0.9789 -> 0.889. Class already solved kept (Lasry's decryption, 2020). 23 Oct 2026, re-read (b22): R154 and R173 read from the complete contemporary interlinear decipherments on the DECODE images, aligned with the figures; six key values corrected or added (key_b22.tsv); all 24 despatches read.

title: Segreteria di Stato (Rome) to the Nuncio in Spain, 24 ciphered despatches, 4 Jan 1718 - 6 Jan 1720, ASV Segr. Stato Spagna 364D (DECODE R154-R177)
system.summary: Undivided digit stream: two-digit homophones for letters and a few syllables, four-digit nomenclator groups prefixed 4, and the single digit 3 as a null.
system.sibling_key: None needed: the same key serves Spagna 364C (items 1-32) and 364D (items 1-24), 1717-1720.
system.notes: Nomenclator runs: 4001-4078 particles and endings; 4079-4296 nouns and names A-R; 4401-4479 S-V; 4485-4531 calendar and day numbers; 4532-4543 and 4552-4563 two parallel Gennaio-Dicembre month runs; 4535-4619 a second alphabetical run A-T; scattered blocks at 4681, 4706, 4870+. Lasry's filed key gives 268 of the 399 four-digit groups used in the corpus; 61 more were recovered in this session, leaving 135 distinct groups (3.4% of nomenclator tokens) without a value. The digit 3 is a null, except when it falls among the three digits following a 4 prefix, where it belongs to the nomenclator group.

outcome.method_basis: Lasry's reconstructed S364 key (24 Oct 2020) and his segmented decipherment of the whole corpus were attached to every DECODE record R154-R177 before the attempt; the project measured that reading and recovered 61 more nomenclator groups from alphabetical brackets and context.

outcome.notes: Solved by George Lasry in October 2020 and already read on the DECODE records when this session began; nothing about the system was open. What is new here is the measurement of that reading and 61 additional nomenclator values that extend his key. Verification detail: coverage measured token by token off Lasry's aligned decipherment; each recovered group rests on two or more independent contexts and usually the alphabetical bracket; 4538=Luglio matches the known date of Alberoni's promotion, 12 July 1717. 22 Oct 2026, reading audit: R154 and R173 decoded, not read; R166, R168, R170 overturned to B; fraction_read 0.9789 -> 0.889. Class already solved kept (Lasry's decryption, 2020). 23 Oct 2026, re-read (b22): R154 and R173 read from the complete contemporary interlinear decipherments on the DECODE images, aligned with the figures; six key values corrected or added (key_b22.tsv); all 24 despatches read.

title: Segreteria di Stato (Rome) to the Nuncio in Spain, 24 ciphered despatches, 4 Jan 1718 - 6 Jan 1720, ASV Segr. Stato Spagna 364D (DECODE R154-R177)
system.summary: Undivided digit stream: two-digit homophones for letters and a few syllables, four-digit nomenclator groups prefixed 4, and the single digit 3 as a null.
system.sibling_key: None needed: the same key serves Spagna 364C (items 1-32) and 364D (items 1-24), 1717-1720.
system.notes: Nomenclator runs: 4001-4078 particles and endings; 4079-4296 nouns and names A-R; 4401-4479 S-V; 4485-4531 calendar and day numbers; 4532-4543 and 4552-4563 two parallel Gennaio-Dicembre month runs; 4535-4619 a second alphabetical run A-T; scattered blocks at 4681, 4706, 4870+. Lasry's filed key gives 268 of the 399 four-digit groups used in the corpus; 61 more were recovered in this session, leaving 135 distinct groups (3.4% of nomenclator tokens) without a value. The digit 3 is a null, except when it falls among the three digits following a 4 prefix, where it belongs to the nomenclator group.

outcome.notes: Solved by George Lasry in October 2020 and already read on the DECODE records when this session began; nothing about the system was open. What is new here is the measurement of that reading and 61 additional nomenclator values that extend his key. Verification detail: coverage measured token by token off Lasry's aligned decipherment; each recovered group rests on two or more independent contexts and usually the alphabetical bracket; 4538=Luglio matches the known date of Alberoni's promotion, 12 July 1717. 22 Oct 2026, reading audit: R154 and R173 decoded, not read; R166, R168, R170 overturned to B; fraction_read 0.9789 -> 0.889. Class already solved kept (Lasry's decryption, 2020). 23 Oct 2026, re-read (b22): R154 and R173 read from the complete contemporary interlinear decipherments on the DECODE images, aligned with the figures; six key values corrected or added (key_b22.tsv); all 24 despatches read.

title: Segreteria di Stato (Rome) to the Nuncio in Spain, 24 ciphered despatches, 4 Jan 1718 - 6 Jan 1720, ASV Segr. Stato Spagna 364D (DECODE R154-R177)
system.summary: Undivided digit stream: two-digit homophones for letters and a few syllables, four-digit nomenclator groups prefixed 4, and the single digit 3 as a null.
system.sibling_key: None needed: the same key serves Spagna 364C (items 1-32) and 364D (items 1-24), 1717-1720.
system.notes: Nomenclator runs: 4001-4078 particles and endings; 4079-4296 nouns and names A-R; 4401-4479 S-V; 4485-4531 calendar and day numbers; 4532-4543 and 4552-4563 two parallel Gennaio-Dicembre month runs; 4535-4619 a second alphabetical run A-T; scattered blocks at 4681, 4706, 4870+. Lasry's filed key gives 268 of the 399 four-digit groups used in the corpus; 61 more were recovered in this session, leaving 135 distinct groups (3.4% of nomenclator tokens) without a value. The digit 3 is a null, except when it falls among the three digits following a 4 prefix, where it belongs to the nomenclator group.

outcome.method_basis: Lasry's reconstructed S364 key (24 Oct 2020) and his segmented decipherment of the whole corpus were attached to every DECODE record R154-R177 before the attempt; the project measured that reading and recovered 61 more nomenclator groups from alphabetical brackets and context.

outcome.verification: key confirms; contemporary decipherment; historical consistency
outcome.notes: Solved by George Lasry in October 2020 and already read on the DECODE records when this session began; nothing about the system was open. What is new here is the measurement of that reading and 61 additional nomenclator values that extend his key. Verification detail: coverage measured token by token off Lasry's aligned decipherment; each recovered group rests on two or more independent contexts and usually the alphabetical bracket; 4538=Luglio matches the known date of Alberoni's promotion, 12 July 1717. 22 Oct 2026, reading audit: R154 and R173 decoded, not read; R166, R168, R170 overturned to B; fraction_read 0.9789 -> 0.889. Class already solved kept (Lasry's decryption, 2020). 23 Oct 2026, re-read (b22): R154 and R173 read from the complete contemporary interlinear decipherments on the DECODE images, aligned with the figures; six key values corrected or added (key_b22.tsv); all 24 despatches read.

title: Segreteria di Stato (Rome) to the Nuncio in Spain, 24 ciphered despatches, 4 Jan 1718 - 6 Jan 1720, ASV Segr. Stato Spagna 364D (DECODE R154-R177)
system.summary: Undivided digit stream: two-digit homophones for letters and a few syllables, four-digit nomenclator groups prefixed 4, and the single digit 3 as a null.
system.sibling_key: None needed: the same key serves Spagna 364C (items 1-32) and 364D (items 1-24), 1717-1720.
system.notes: Nomenclator runs: 4001-4078 particles and endings; 4079-4296 nouns and names A-R; 4401-4479 S-V; 4485-4531 calendar and day numbers; 4532-4543 and 4552-4563 two parallel Gennaio-Dicembre month runs; 4535-4619 a second alphabetical run A-T; scattered blocks at 4681, 4706, 4870+. Lasry's filed key gives 268 of the 399 four-digit groups used in the corpus; 61 more were recovered in this session, leaving 135 distinct groups (3.4% of nomenclator tokens) without a value. The digit 3 is a null, except when it falls among the three digits following a 4 prefix, where it belongs to the nomenclator group.

outcome.method_basis: Lasry's reconstructed S364 key (24 Oct 2020) and his segmented decipherment of the whole corpus were attached to every DECODE record R154-R177 before the attempt; the project measured that reading and recovered 61 more nomenclator groups from alphabetical brackets and context.

outcome.notes: Solved by George Lasry in October 2020 and already read on the DECODE records when this session began; nothing about the system was open. What is new here is the measurement of that reading and 61 additional nomenclator values that extend his key. Verification detail: coverage measured token by token off Lasry's aligned decipherment; each recovered group rests on two or more independent contexts and usually the alphabetical bracket; 4538=Luglio matches the known date of Alberoni's promotion, 12 July 1717. 22 Oct 2026, reading audit: R154 and R173 decoded, not read; R166, R168, R170 overturned to B; fraction_read 0.9789 -> 0.889. Class already solved kept (Lasry's decryption, 2020). 23 Oct 2026, re-read (b22): R154 and R173 read from the complete contemporary interlinear decipherments on the DECODE images, aligned with the figures; six key values corrected or added (key_b22.tsv); all 24 despatches read.

title: Segreteria di Stato (Rome) to the Nuncio in Spain, 24 ciphered despatches, 4 Jan 1718 - 6 Jan 1720, ASV Segr. Stato Spagna 364D (DECODE R154-R177)
system.summary: Undivided digit stream: two-digit homophones for letters and a few syllables, four-digit nomenclator groups prefixed 4, and the single digit 3 as a null.
system.sibling_key: None needed: the same key serves Spagna 364C (items 1-32) and 364D (items 1-24), 1717-1720.
system.notes: Nomenclator runs: 4001-4078 particles and endings; 4079-4296 nouns and names A-R; 4401-4479 S-V; 4485-4531 calendar and day numbers; 4532-4543 and 4552-4563 two parallel Gennaio-Dicembre month runs; 4535-4619 a second alphabetical run A-T; scattered blocks at 4681, 4706, 4870+. Lasry's filed key gives 268 of the 399 four-digit groups used in the corpus; 61 more were recovered in this session, leaving 135 distinct groups (3.4% of nomenclator tokens) without a value. The digit 3 is a null, except when it falls among the three digits following a 4 prefix, where it belongs to the nomenclator group.

outcome.notes: Solved by George Lasry in October 2020 and already read on the DECODE records when this session began; nothing about the system was open. What is new here is the measurement of that reading and 61 additional nomenclator values that extend his key. Verification detail: coverage measured token by token off Lasry's aligned decipherment; each recovered group rests on two or more independent contexts and usually the alphabetical bracket; 4538=Luglio matches the known date of Alberoni's promotion, 12 July 1717. 22 Oct 2026, reading audit: R154 and R173 decoded, not read; R166, R168, R170 overturned to B; fraction_read 0.9789 -> 0.889. Class already solved kept (Lasry's decryption, 2020). 23 Oct 2026, re-read (b22): R154 and R173 read from the complete contemporary interlinear decipherments on the DECODE images, aligned with the figures; six key values corrected or added (key_b22.tsv); all 24 despatches read.

title: Segreteria di Stato (Rome) to the Nuncio in Spain, 24 ciphered despatches, 4 Jan 1718 - 6 Jan 1720, ASV Segr. Stato Spagna 364D (DECODE R154-R177)
system.summary: Undivided digit stream: two-digit homophones for letters and a few syllables, four-digit nomenclator groups prefixed 4, and the single digit 3 as a null.
system.sibling_key: None needed: the same key serves Spagna 364C (items 1-32) and 364D (items 1-24), 1717-1720.
system.notes: Nomenclator runs: 4001-4078 particles and endings; 4079-4296 nouns and names A-R; 4401-4479 S-V; 4485-4531 calendar and day numbers; 4532-4543 and 4552-4563 two parallel Gennaio-Dicembre month runs; 4535-4619 a second alphabetical run A-T; scattered blocks at 4681, 4706, 4870+. Lasry's filed key gives 268 of the 399 four-digit groups used in the corpus; 61 more were recovered in this session, leaving 135 distinct groups (3.4% of nomenclator tokens) without a value. The digit 3 is a null, except when it falls among the three digits following a 4 prefix, where it belongs to the nomenclator group.

outcome.method_basis: Lasry's reconstructed S364 key (24 Oct 2020) and his segmented decipherment of the whole corpus were attached to every DECODE record R154-R177 before the attempt; the project measured that reading and recovered 61 more nomenclator groups from alphabetical brackets and context.

outcome.notes: Solved by George Lasry in October 2020 and already read on the DECODE records when this session began; nothing about the system was open. What is new here is the measurement of that reading and 61 additional nomenclator values that extend his key. Verification detail: coverage measured token by token off Lasry's aligned decipherment; each recovered group rests on two or more independent contexts and usually the alphabetical bracket; 4538=Luglio matches the known date of Alberoni's promotion, 12 July 1717. 22 Oct 2026, reading audit: R154 and R173 decoded, not read; R166, R168, R170 overturned to B; fraction_read 0.9789 -> 0.889. Class already solved kept (Lasry's decryption, 2020). 23 Oct 2026, re-read (b22): R154 and R173 read from the complete contemporary interlinear decipherments on the DECODE images, aligned with the figures; six key values corrected or added (key_b22.tsv); all 24 despatches read.

title: Segreteria di Stato (Rome) to the Nuncio in Spain, 24 ciphered despatches, 4 Jan 1718 - 6 Jan 1720, ASV Segr. Stato Spagna 364D (DECODE R154-R177)
system.summary: Undivided digit stream: two-digit homophones for letters and a few syllables, four-digit nomenclator groups prefixed 4, and the single digit 3 as a null.
system.sibling_key: None needed: the same key serves Spagna 364C (items 1-32) and 364D (items 1-24), 1717-1720.
system.notes: Nomenclator runs: 4001-4078 particles and endings; 4079-4296 nouns and names A-R; 4401-4479 S-V; 4485-4531 calendar and day numbers; 4532-4543 and 4552-4563 two parallel Gennaio-Dicembre month runs; 4535-4619 a second alphabetical run A-T; scattered blocks at 4681, 4706, 4870+. Lasry's filed key gives 268 of the 399 four-digit groups used in the corpus; 61 more were recovered in this session, leaving 135 distinct groups (3.4% of nomenclator tokens) without a value. The digit 3 is a null, except when it falls among the three digits following a 4 prefix, where it belongs to the nomenclator group.

outcome.notes: Solved by George Lasry in October 2020 and already read on the DECODE records when this session began; nothing about the system was open. What is new here is the measurement of that reading and 61 additional nomenclator values that extend his key. Verification detail: coverage measured token by token off Lasry's aligned decipherment; each recovered group rests on two or more independent contexts and usually the alphabetical bracket; 4538=Luglio matches the known date of Alberoni's promotion, 12 July 1717. 22 Oct 2026, reading audit: R154 and R173 decoded, not read; R166, R168, R170 overturned to B; fraction_read 0.9789 -> 0.889. Class already solved kept (Lasry's decryption, 2020). 23 Oct 2026, re-read (b22): R154 and R173 read from the complete contemporary interlinear decipherments on the DECODE images, aligned with the figures; six key values corrected or added (key_b22.tsv); all 24 despatches read.
