outcome.method_basis: 'Mascon's cipher' was reconstructed from fr. 3053 by Tomokiyo and tabulated by Lasry (2023, GL.htm, for fr. 3071 f. 9); the project applied it through macon_key.md to the seven fr. 3053 records and the fr. 3071 no. 4 letter, and corrected values from glossed lines in the volume.
outcome.contribution: transcription; key extended or corrected; sender or date identified
outcome.notes: About 95% of the cipher letters of the seven fr. 3053 records read after a shape-true re-transcription from the Gallica native scans (pass 5, 22 Sept 2026), checked against every contemporary clear text (CER 3-8%); the fr. 3071 no. 4 letter of 11 Apr 1537 read apart from short spots, its f. 9v passage confirmed by the contemporary slip f. 9bis. Nothing is physically unreadable in fr. 3053; the residue is ambiguous sign runs and names. Key recovered (Tomokiyo/Lasry Mascon's cipher, corrected and split by sign shape). R4248, in another cipher, is targets/r4248/. 22 Oct 2026, reading audit: R4234 and R4239 overturned to B; fr. 3071 no. 4 decoded, not read; fraction_read 0.95 -> about 0.91.

system.summary: Homophonic substitution on digit-like graphic signs, one sign per letter, with doubled-letter signs, nulls and three two-digit code groups.
system.sibling_key: 'Mascon's cipher' as reconstructed by S. Tomokiyo from fr. 3053 and tabulated by G. Lasry (2023) for BnF fr. 3071 f. 9; working table macon_key.md (moved here from targets/gramont1529/), used with corrections.
system.notes: Code groups 20 = l'Empereur, 30 = pape, 40 = roy, and no others in the seven fr. 3053 records or the fr. 3071 letter. The barred-cross family of signs reads F, P, O, U, V and D in the same hand and is separable only by context; the big curly X is Q/U, not N, contrary to the working table. distinct_symbols counts the fr. 3053 records. The f. 85 record (R4248) is in a second, unrelated fr. 3053 cipher and is its own entry since 14 Oct 2026 (targets/r4248/).
conditions.prior_solution.where: Contemporary marginal and interlinear decipherments of some fr. 3053 passages in the volume itself, and the slip f. 9bis deciphering the f. 9v passage of fr. 3071 no. 4. No printed or online plaintext: Tomokiyo and Lasry publish the key only. Lasry also decoded fr. 3071 no. 4 in 2023, unpublished (Lasry, 21 Sept 2026); no Lasry decipherment of the fr. 3053 letters is recorded.
conditions.inputs: images; published key; sibling key; cleartext context
conditions.human_role: nothing beyond setting the target; the DECODE session cookie already in the repository served the images

outcome.method_basis: 'Mascon's cipher' was reconstructed from fr. 3053 by Tomokiyo and tabulated by Lasry (2023, GL.htm, for fr. 3071 f. 9); the project applied it through macon_key.md to the seven fr. 3053 records and the fr. 3071 no. 4 letter, and corrected values from glossed lines in the volume.
outcome.contribution: transcription; key extended or corrected; sender or date identified
outcome.notes: About 95% of the cipher letters of the seven fr. 3053 records read after a shape-true re-transcription from the Gallica native scans (pass 5, 22 Sept 2026), checked against every contemporary clear text (CER 3-8%); the fr. 3071 no. 4 letter of 11 Apr 1537 read apart from short spots, its f. 9v passage confirmed by the contemporary slip f. 9bis. Nothing is physically unreadable in fr. 3053; the residue is ambiguous sign runs and names. Key recovered (Tomokiyo/Lasry Mascon's cipher, corrected and split by sign shape). R4248, in another cipher, is targets/r4248/. 22 Oct 2026, reading audit: R4234 and R4239 overturned to B; fr. 3071 no. 4 decoded, not read; fraction_read 0.95 -> about 0.91.

title: Charles Hémard de Denonville, cardinal de Mâcon, Rome and Orvieto to Anne de Montmorency, 1536-37, in Mascon's cipher (BnF fr. 3053, DECODE R4233-R4247; BnF fr. 3071 no. 4)
system.summary: Homophonic substitution on digit-like graphic signs, one sign per letter, with doubled-letter signs, nulls and three two-digit code groups.
system.sibling_key: 'Mascon's cipher' as reconstructed by S. Tomokiyo from fr. 3053 and tabulated by G. Lasry (2023) for BnF fr. 3071 f. 9; working table macon_key.md (moved here from targets/gramont1529/), used with corrections.
system.notes: Code groups 20 = l'Empereur, 30 = pape, 40 = roy, and no others in the seven fr. 3053 records or the fr. 3071 letter. The barred-cross family of signs reads F, P, O, U, V and D in the same hand and is separable only by context; the big curly X is Q/U, not N, contrary to the working table. distinct_symbols counts the fr. 3053 records. The f. 85 record (R4248) is in a second, unrelated fr. 3053 cipher and is its own entry since 14 Oct 2026 (targets/r4248/).
conditions.prior_solution.where: Contemporary marginal and interlinear decipherments of some fr. 3053 passages in the volume itself, and the slip f. 9bis deciphering the f. 9v passage of fr. 3071 no. 4. Lasry also decoded fr. 3071 no. 4 in 2023, unpublished (Lasry, 21 Sept 2026); no Lasry decipherment of the fr. 3053 letters is recorded.

title: Charles Hémard de Denonville, cardinal de Mâcon, Rome and Orvieto to Anne de Montmorency, 1536-37, in Mascon's cipher (BnF fr. 3053, DECODE R4233-R4247; BnF fr. 3071 no. 4)
system.summary: Homophonic substitution on digit-like graphic signs, one sign per letter, with doubled-letter signs, nulls and three two-digit code groups.
system.sibling_key: 'Mascon's cipher' as reconstructed by S. Tomokiyo from fr. 3053 and tabulated by G. Lasry (2023) for BnF fr. 3071 f. 9; working table macon_key.md (moved here from targets/gramont1529/), used with corrections.
system.notes: Code groups 20 = l'Empereur, 30 = pape, 40 = roy, and no others in the seven fr. 3053 records or the fr. 3071 letter. The barred-cross family of signs reads F, P, O, U, V and D in the same hand and is separable only by context; the big curly X is Q/U, not N, contrary to the working table. distinct_symbols counts the fr. 3053 records. The f. 85 record (R4248) is in a second, unrelated fr. 3053 cipher and is its own entry since 14 Oct 2026 (targets/r4248/).
conditions.prior_solution.where: Contemporary marginal and interlinear decipherments of some fr. 3053 passages in the volume itself, and the slip f. 9bis deciphering the f. 9v passage of fr. 3071 no. 4. No printed or online plaintext: Tomokiyo and Lasry publish the key only. Lasry also decoded fr. 3071 no. 4 in 2023, unpublished (Lasry, 21 Sept 2026); no Lasry decipherment of the fr. 3053 letters is recorded.
conditions.inputs: images; published key; sibling key; cleartext context
conditions.human_role: nothing beyond setting the target; the DECODE session cookie already in the repository served the images

outcome.method_basis: 'Mascon's cipher' was reconstructed from fr. 3053 by Tomokiyo and tabulated by Lasry (2023, GL.htm, for fr. 3071 f. 9); the project applied it through macon_key.md to the seven fr. 3053 records and the fr. 3071 no. 4 letter, and corrected values from glossed lines in the volume.
outcome.contribution: transcription; key extended or corrected; sender or date identified
outcome.notes: About 95% of the cipher letters of the seven fr. 3053 records read after a shape-true re-transcription from the Gallica native scans (pass 5, 22 Sept 2026), checked against every contemporary clear text (CER 3-8%); the fr. 3071 no. 4 letter of 11 Apr 1537 read apart from short spots, its f. 9v passage confirmed by the contemporary slip f. 9bis. Nothing is physically unreadable in fr. 3053; the residue is ambiguous sign runs and names. Key recovered (Tomokiyo/Lasry Mascon's cipher, corrected and split by sign shape). R4248, in another cipher, is targets/r4248/. 22 Oct 2026, reading audit: R4234 and R4239 overturned to B; fr. 3071 no. 4 decoded, not read; fraction_read 0.95 -> about 0.91.

system.sibling_key: Juan Manuel's 1522 Rome cipher (DECODE R9499-R9529), same design, different values; also reconstructed by Tomokiyo. R9605 and R9613 carry full contemporary decipherments on leaves facing their cipher, and are the calibration source for the hand.
conditions.prior_solution.where: S. Tomokiyo, 'Correspondence in Cipher of Imperial Ambassadors Alonso Sanchez and Juan Manuel (1522)', https://cryptiana.web.fc2.com/code/AlonsoSanchez.htm, posted 6 September 2025. Gives the substitution alphabet, ~177 code groups, and the deciphered opening lines of R9593-R9632. Also: English abstracts of 14 of these letters, made from the contemporary decipherings, in G. A. Bergenroth, Calendar of State Papers, Spain, vol. 2 (1866), nos. 429-500 (R9635 = no. 476); found 2026-09-21, after the partial reading of R9635.
conditions.human_role: supplied the DECODE login cookie (reused from an earlier target); set the goal.
conditions.tools: PIL crops/upscaling of DECODE images; ordering analysis of the nomenclator (key_codes.tsv)
outcome.method_basis: 23 Oct 2026 (b23): R9635 is read from its contemporary decipherment, a clear copy on f. 22r of the DECODE record, checked against the figures of ff. 20r-20v with Tomokiyo's 2025 key. R9653 has no decipherment: its cipher (f. 299r foot and f. 299v) was read sign by sign with Tomokiyo's key and builds sentences only in its first paragraph, so it stays decoded, not read. r2i (23 Oct 2026): R9613 and R9641 read from contemporary decipherments imaged on DECODE (R9613 ff. 206-207; R9641's on ff. 187-188 under R9642), each checked against its cipher with Tomokiyo's key; R9635's torn passage filled from its own cipher.
outcome.contribution: transcription; key extended or corrected; sender or date identified; catalogue correction
outcome.verification: key confirms; contemporary decipherment; historical consistency
outcome.notes: The cipher itself was already solved and published by Tomokiyo in September 2025, so this is not a break. Added here: the catalogue entry's shelfmark, date range and authorship corrected; the ordering rule of the nomenclator, and from it a c-block numeral series of which cab = xv, cef = xxvi and cif = xxvii are confirmed in text and were not in the published key; and first readings of parts of R9635 and R9653, both outside Tomokiyo's coverage. fraction_read is the share of code groups resolved on the two leaves worked; the spelled-out letter runs and the other 27 records are open. Also established that the nine Lope Hurtado de Mendoza records in the group are in a different cipher, which deserves its own target. The R9605 calibration fixes the sign values against ground truth but does not by itself unlock the unread pages: the binding constraint is the transcription of the cursive shapes, which differ between scribes, and that has to be done glyph by glyph on the image. An edition pass against the published key then began (edition/), reading about a third of R9635 f. 20r continuously and adding lel = 'puede' to the key.

title: Alonso Sánchez (Venice) to Charles V, 1522 — RAH Salazar 9/23–9/26, DECODE R9593–R9657
system.summary: Homophonic substitution alphabet with three nulls, plus a nomenclator of consonant-vowel-consonant code groups assigned in alphabetical order of the plaintext.
system.sibling_key: Juan Manuel's 1522 Rome cipher (DECODE R9499-R9529), same design, different values; also reconstructed by Tomokiyo. R9605 and R9613 carry full contemporary decipherments on leaves facing their cipher, and are the calibration source for the hand.
conditions.prior_solution.where: S. Tomokiyo, 'Correspondence in Cipher of Imperial Ambassadors Alonso Sanchez and Juan Manuel (1522)', https://cryptiana.web.fc2.com/code/AlonsoSanchez.htm, posted 6 September 2025. Gives the substitution alphabet, ~177 code groups, and the deciphered opening lines of R9593-R9632. Also: English abstracts of 14 of these letters, made from the contemporary decipherings, in G. A. Bergenroth, Calendar of State Papers, Spain, vol. 2 (1866), nos. 429-500 (R9635 = no. 476); found 2026-09-21, after the partial reading of R9635.

outcome.method_basis: 23 Oct 2026 (b23): R9635 is read from its contemporary decipherment, a clear copy on f. 22r of the DECODE record, checked against the figures of ff. 20r-20v with Tomokiyo's 2025 key. R9653 has no decipherment: its cipher (f. 299r foot and f. 299v) was read sign by sign with Tomokiyo's key and builds sentences only in its first paragraph, so it stays decoded, not read. r2i (23 Oct 2026): R9613 and R9641 read from contemporary decipherments imaged on DECODE (R9613 ff. 206-207; R9641's on ff. 187-188 under R9642), each checked against its cipher with Tomokiyo's key; R9635's torn passage filled from its own cipher.
outcome.contribution: transcription; key extended or corrected; sender or date identified; catalogue correction
outcome.verification: key confirms; contemporary decipherment; historical consistency
outcome.notes: The cipher itself was already solved and published by Tomokiyo in September 2025, so this is not a break. Added here: the catalogue entry's shelfmark, date range and authorship corrected; the ordering rule of the nomenclator, and from it a c-block numeral series of which cab = xv, cef = xxvi and cif = xxvii are confirmed in text and were not in the published key; and first readings of parts of R9635 and R9653, both outside Tomokiyo's coverage. fraction_read is the share of code groups resolved on the two leaves worked; the spelled-out letter runs and the other 27 records are open. Also established that the nine Lope Hurtado de Mendoza records in the group are in a different cipher, which deserves its own target. The R9605 calibration fixes the sign values against ground truth but does not by itself unlock the unread pages: the binding constraint is the transcription of the cursive shapes, which differ between scribes, and that has to be done glyph by glyph on the image. An edition pass against the published key then began (edition/), reading about a third of R9635 f. 20r continuously and adding lel = 'puede' to the key.

outcome.notes: The cipher itself was already solved and published by Tomokiyo in September 2025, so this is not a break. Added here: the catalogue entry's shelfmark, date range and authorship corrected; the ordering rule of the nomenclator, and from it a c-block numeral series of which cab = xv, cef = xxvi and cif = xxvii are confirmed in text and were not in the published key; and first readings of parts of R9635 and R9653, both outside Tomokiyo's coverage. fraction_read is the share of code groups resolved on the two leaves worked; the spelled-out letter runs and the other 27 records are open. Also established that the nine Lope Hurtado de Mendoza records in the group are in a different cipher, which deserves its own target. The R9605 calibration fixes the sign values against ground truth but does not by itself unlock the unread pages: the binding constraint is the transcription of the cursive shapes, which differ between scribes, and that has to be done glyph by glyph on the image. An edition pass against the published key then began (edition/), reading about a third of R9635 f. 20r continuously and adding lel = 'puede' to the key.

title: Alonso Sánchez (Venice) to Charles V, May–August 1523 — RAH Salazar 9/28, DECODE R9670–R9770
system.summary: Homophonic substitution alphabet with three nulls, plus a nomenclator of consonant-vowel-consonant code groups assigned in alphabetical order of the plaintext.
system.sibling_key: Juan Manuel's 1522 Rome cipher (DECODE R9499-R9529), same design, different values; also reconstructed by Tomokiyo. R9605 and R9613 carry full contemporary decipherments on leaves facing their cipher, and are the calibration source for the hand.
conditions.prior_solution.where: G. A. Bergenroth, Calendar of State Papers, Spain, vol. 2 (1866), nos. 549, 552, 554, 558: English abstracts from the contemporary decipherings. Key: S. Tomokiyo, cryptiana.web.fc2.com/code/AlonsoSanchez.htm (2025), extended in this project's sanchez1522.
conditions.inputs: images; published key; sibling key; published reading; cleartext context
conditions.human_role: set the goal; the DECODE login cookie was reused from an earlier target.
conditions.tools: DECODE record scraper and image fetch (decode/); targets/sanchez1522/decode_tokens.py
outcome.method_basis: The code groups were read with Sánchez's own 1522 key (Tomokiyo, cryptiana AlonsoSanchez.htm 2025, extended in sanchez1522), unchanged into 1523; the May-June despatches were already calendared by Bergenroth (CSP Spain 2, nos. 549-558) from the contemporary decipherings.
outcome.contribution: transcription; sender or date identified; catalogue correction
outcome.verification: contemporary decipherment; key confirms; historical consistency
outcome.notes: The May–June despatches were deciphered at the time and calendared in English by Bergenroth in 1866; the key was published by Tomokiyo in 2025. Added here: the records identified against the Calendar, the recipient corrected (Charles V), the 1522 key shown to hold in 1523, and (23 Oct 2026) the two uncalendared August letters read in full from contemporary decipherments found on neighbouring leaves (f. 567r on DECODE R9768 for R9767; f. 574r on R9770 for the joint letter R9769/R9770), each checked group by group against the cipher. New code value pem = -mos.

New code value pem = -mos.

title: Alonso Sánchez (Venice) to Charles V, May–August 1523 — RAH Salazar 9/28, DECODE R9670–R9770
system.summary: Homophonic substitution alphabet with three nulls, plus a nomenclator of consonant-vowel-consonant code groups assigned in alphabetical order of the plaintext.
system.sibling_key: Juan Manuel's 1522 Rome cipher (DECODE R9499-R9529), same design, different values; also reconstructed by Tomokiyo. R9605 and R9613 carry full contemporary decipherments on leaves facing their cipher, and are the calibration source for the hand.
conditions.prior_solution.where: G. A. Bergenroth, Calendar of State Papers, Spain, vol. 2 (1866), nos. 549, 552, 554, 558: English abstracts from the contemporary decipherings. Key: S. Tomokiyo, cryptiana.web.fc2.com/code/AlonsoSanchez.htm (2025), extended in this project's sanchez1522.
conditions.inputs: images; published key; sibling key; published reading; cleartext context
conditions.human_role: set the goal; the DECODE login cookie was reused from an earlier target.
conditions.tools: DECODE record scraper and image fetch (decode/); targets/sanchez1522/decode_tokens.py
outcome.method_basis: The code groups were read with Sánchez's own 1522 key (Tomokiyo, cryptiana AlonsoSanchez.htm 2025, extended in sanchez1522), unchanged into 1523; the May-June despatches were already calendared by Bergenroth (CSP Spain 2, nos. 549-558) from the contemporary decipherings.
outcome.contribution: transcription; sender or date identified; catalogue correction
outcome.verification: contemporary decipherment; key confirms; historical consistency
outcome.notes: The May–June despatches were deciphered at the time and calendared in English by Bergenroth in 1866; the key was published by Tomokiyo in 2025. Added here: the records identified against the Calendar, the recipient corrected (Charles V), the 1522 key shown to hold in 1523, and (23 Oct 2026) the two uncalendared August letters read in full from contemporary decipherments found on neighbouring leaves (f. 567r on DECODE R9768 for R9767; f. 574r on R9770 for the joint letter R9769/R9770), each checked group by group against the cipher. New code value pem = -mos.

title: Alonso Sánchez (Venice) to Charles V, May–August 1523 — RAH Salazar 9/28, DECODE R9670–R9770
system.summary: Homophonic substitution alphabet with three nulls, plus a nomenclator of consonant-vowel-consonant code groups assigned in alphabetical order of the plaintext.
system.sibling_key: Juan Manuel's 1522 Rome cipher (DECODE R9499-R9529), same design, different values; also reconstructed by Tomokiyo. R9605 and R9613 carry full contemporary decipherments on leaves facing their cipher, and are the calibration source for the hand.
conditions.prior_solution.where: G. A. Bergenroth, Calendar of State Papers, Spain, vol. 2 (1866), nos. 549, 552, 554, 558: English abstracts from the contemporary decipherings. Key: S. Tomokiyo, cryptiana.web.fc2.com/code/AlonsoSanchez.htm (2025), extended in this project's sanchez1522.
conditions.inputs: images; published key; sibling key; published reading; cleartext context
conditions.human_role: set the goal; the DECODE login cookie was reused from an earlier target.
conditions.tools: DECODE record scraper and image fetch (decode/); targets/sanchez1522/decode_tokens.py
outcome.method_basis: The code groups were read with Sánchez's own 1522 key (Tomokiyo, cryptiana AlonsoSanchez.htm 2025, extended in sanchez1522), unchanged into 1523; the May-June despatches were already calendared by Bergenroth (CSP Spain 2, nos. 549-558) from the contemporary decipherings.
outcome.contribution: transcription; sender or date identified; catalogue correction
outcome.verification: contemporary decipherment; key confirms; historical consistency
outcome.notes: The May–June despatches were deciphered at the time and calendared in English by Bergenroth in 1866; the key was published by Tomokiyo in 2025. Added here: the records identified against the Calendar, the recipient corrected (Charles V), the 1522 key shown to hold in 1523, and (23 Oct 2026) the two uncalendared August letters read in full from contemporary decipherments found on neighbouring leaves (f. 567r on DECODE R9768 for R9767; f. 574r on R9770 for the joint letter R9769/R9770), each checked group by group against the cipher. New code value pem = -mos.

system.summary: German clear text with a 2-digit homophonic letter table in alphabetical blocks of three (a=7-9, b=10-12 ... no j, v), 3-digit codes for persons, courts and words (the 500s an alphabetical word list), and dotted letter signs that are a code for small words (o. = der).

system.notes: 79 = z, 70 = w, 76-78 = y; 67-69 serve for v and w. 'Distinct symbols' is the measured count over the Schenck file (letter numbers and codes).

system.sibling_key: Büchi II ciphered letters in the same correspondence (nos. 530, 543, 585, 586, 596, 599, 601 …), several Schiner–England letters with interlinear decipherment (e.g. 585, Vit. B XIX f. 342); keys never printed. The only sign-level fact known is Brewer's monogram for 'Vestrae Majestati'.
system.notes: symbol_kind 'symbols' rests on Brewer's 'monogram in cipher' only.
conditions.prior_solution.where: Büchi, Korrespondenzen und Akten II (1925), no. 541: full decipherment by Büchi and Schiess; partial reading in L&P II 2044 (1864); content abstracted in 1516 (L&P II 2045). Missed by the 22 Sept 2026 sweep, which checked L&P and Tomokiyo only.
conditions.human_role: Project-level: set up Claude Code with Opus 5.5 and posed the target with /goal from the catalogue entry (290), asking for a reading past 95% if possible. Mid-session the user asked for the HathiTrust bot check to be bypassed; that was declined and the edition was reached through e-Helvetica instead. No target-specific intervention.
conditions.tools: BL searcharchives catalogue; British History Online (L&P); e-Helvetica (Swiss National Library) PDF of Büchi II; PyMuPDF page rendering
outcome.method_basis: Büchi and Schiess printed the full decipherment in Korrespondenzen und Akten II (1925) no. 541, pp. 67-72 (cipher in italics); the leaf is not digitised, so nothing was deciphered here.
outcome.notes: Deciphered by Büchi and Schiess (1925); nothing deciphered here. Added: the 1925 reading found for an entry listed as unread; the 14 cipher stretches located, counted and translated; L&P shown to print 6 of them and the 1516 abstract shown to confirm their content; old and new foliation reconciled (f. 131 = f. 129).

doc.route: Cardinal Matthäus Schiner, Trent -> Henry VIII, London

title: A correspondent at Beaupréau to Ségur, July 1583, BnF 500 de Colbert 401 f. 143 (a third key of the Navarre design)
system.summary: A numeric cipher of the same chancery design as the ff. 233 and f. 321 keys by the writer's own description ('lettres, syllabes, doubles, nulles ... Les noms sont en lettres et syllabes'), with different values; figures up to 156 and letter-written signs (Pa, a, H, L, I).
system.sibling_key: ff. 233 key (key A, segur) and Tomokiyo's f. 321 key (navarre1586): same design, neither fits f. 143.
system.notes: Different key from ff. 233/239/288v per NOTES (it does not decode with key_v4.json); too short for the structured annealers, whose floor for this design lies between about 120 and 460 tokens.
conditions.prior_solution.where: George Lasry's saved decryptions of 15 Oct 2024 cover ff. 143, 233, 239 and 288v (his note to the project, Oct 2026); unpublished; earlier reported 25 Sept 2026 as an independent 2024 solution.

outcome.notes: Attempted, not solved: transcribed and identified (a letter to Ségur from Beaupréau, July 1583, describing its own cipher), too short to attack. Lasry's saved decryption of 15 Oct 2024 covers it.

system.notes: Key: Add MS 4136 f. 179 'Sr Thomas Smith's Cipher' (DECODE R9261 p.1), Forbes's copy. 'enos' is Ambassador, not a null.

system.summary: Homophonic alphabet of symbols (a-m) and digits 2-10 marked bare/dot/colon (n-p, r-s, t-u-y), dotted-letter word codes, about 30 name symbols and a list of null words (English ports, 'and', 'bycause').

system.sibling_key: Throckmorton's and Croft's ciphers are filed with it (R9260, R9262, R9261 p.2); not used.
system.notes: Key: Add MS 4136 f. 179 'Sr Thomas Smith's Cipher' (DECODE R9261 p.1), Forbes's copy. 'enos' is Ambassador, not a null.
conditions.prior_solution.where: Contemporary decipherments on the SP 70 originals; 1562/3 letters printed in full by Forbes, A Full View (1740-41); later letters summarised in CSP Foreign vols 6-8 (1869-71)

system.summary: Homophonic alphabet of symbols (a-m) and digits 2-10 marked bare/dot/colon (n-p, r-s, t-u-y), dotted-letter word codes, about 30 name symbols and a list of null words (English ports, 'and', 'bycause').

system.sibling_key: Throckmorton's and Croft's ciphers are filed with it (R9260, R9262, R9261 p.2); not used.
system.notes: Key: Add MS 4136 f. 179 'Sr Thomas Smith's Cipher' (DECODE R9261 p.1), Forbes's copy. 'enos' is Ambassador, not a null.
conditions.prior_solution.where: Contemporary decipherments on the SP 70 originals; 1562/3 letters printed in full by Forbes, A Full View (1740-41); later letters summarised in CSP Foreign vols 6-8 (1869-71)

system.summary: Homophonic alphabet of symbols (a-m) and digits 2-10 marked bare/dot/colon (n-p, r-s, t-u-y), dotted-letter word codes, about 30 name symbols and a list of null words (English ports, 'and', 'bycause').

system.sibling_key: Throckmorton's and Croft's ciphers are filed with it (R9260, R9262, R9261 p.2); not used.
system.notes: Key: Add MS 4136 f. 179 'Sr Thomas Smith's Cipher' (DECODE R9261 p.1), Forbes's copy. 'enos' is Ambassador, not a null.
conditions.prior_solution.where: Contemporary decipherments on the SP 70 originals; 1562/3 letters printed in full by Forbes, A Full View (1740-41); later letters summarised in CSP Foreign vols 6-8 (1869-71)

system.summary: Homophonic alphabet of symbols (a-m) and digits 2-10 marked bare/dot/colon (n-p, r-s, t-u-y), dotted-letter word codes, about 30 name symbols and a list of null words (English ports, 'and', 'bycause').

system.sibling_key: Throckmorton's and Croft's ciphers are filed with it (R9260, R9262, R9261 p.2); not used.
system.notes: Key: Add MS 4136 f. 179 'Sr Thomas Smith's Cipher' (DECODE R9261 p.1), Forbes's copy. 'enos' is Ambassador, not a null.
conditions.prior_solution.where: Contemporary decipherments on the SP 70 originals; 1562/3 letters printed in full by Forbes, A Full View (1740-41); later letters summarised in CSP Foreign vols 6-8 (1869-71)

system.summary: Homophonic alphabet of symbols (a-m) and digits 2-10 marked bare/dot/colon (n-p, r-s, t-u-y), dotted-letter word codes, about 30 name symbols and a list of null words (English ports, 'and', 'bycause').

system.sibling_key: Throckmorton's and Croft's ciphers are filed with it (R9260, R9262, R9261 p.2); not used.
system.notes: Key: Add MS 4136 f. 179 'Sr Thomas Smith's Cipher' (DECODE R9261 p.1), Forbes's copy. 'enos' is Ambassador, not a null.
conditions.prior_solution.where: Contemporary decipherments on the SP 70 originals; 1562/3 letters printed in full by Forbes, A Full View (1740-41); later letters summarised in CSP Foreign vols 6-8 (1869-71)

system.summary: Homophonic alphabet of symbols (a-m) and digits 2-10 marked bare/dot/colon (n-p, r-s, t-u-y), dotted-letter word codes, about 30 name symbols and a list of null words (English ports, 'and', 'bycause').

system.sibling_key: Throckmorton's and Croft's ciphers are filed with it (R9260, R9262, R9261 p.2); not used.
system.notes: Key: Add MS 4136 f. 179 'Sr Thomas Smith's Cipher' (DECODE R9261 p.1), Forbes's copy. 'enos' is Ambassador, not a null.
conditions.prior_solution.where: Contemporary decipherments on the SP 70 originals; 1562/3 letters printed in full by Forbes, A Full View (1740-41); later letters summarised in CSP Foreign vols 6-8 (1869-71)

system.summary: Homophonic alphabet of symbols (a-m) and digits 2-10 marked bare/dot/colon (n-p, r-s, t-u-y), dotted-letter word codes, about 30 name symbols and a list of null words (English ports, 'and', 'bycause').

system.sibling_key: Throckmorton's and Croft's ciphers are filed with it (R9260, R9262, R9261 p.2); not used.
system.notes: Key: Add MS 4136 f. 179 'Sr Thomas Smith's Cipher' (DECODE R9261 p.1), Forbes's copy. 'enos' is Ambassador, not a null.

system.summary: Homophonic alphabet of symbols (a-m) and digits 2-10 marked bare/dot/colon (n-p, r-s, t-u-y), dotted-letter word codes, about 30 name symbols and a list of null words (English ports, 'and', 'bycause').

title: 'Nicle'(?) at Nancy to 'Monsieur', December, 17th c., French homophonic pigpen, TNA SP 106/10 ff. 241-243 (DECODE R927)
system.summary: Homophonic pigpen: cell shape (with optional inner stroke) plus 1-3 dots; common letters have several signs.
system.sibling_key: unknown
system.notes: Shapes A-I = the nine pigpen cells (A=RB, B=LRB, C=LB, D=TRB, E=box, F=TLB, G=TR, H=TLR, I=TL in archive orientation), K = stem with a middle bar, X = rare extra sign; * = inner stroke; digit = dot count. Two signs are polyphones resolved by context: C1 = f/q, F2 = l/h. Special signs: '@' (circle/9) and a numeral-like sign, plus the number 67 written in clear in the cipher on f. 241.
conditions.prior_solution.where: Sheila Richards, Secret Writings (1973), as reported by G. Lasry (email 25 Sept 2026); the book was not seen here and a web search found no bibliographic record.
conditions.human_role: unknown
conditions.tools: unknown
outcome.method_basis: The homophonic pigpen key was built by annealing (hc3.py) on a hand transcription of f. 243 until French emerged, then fixed with guessed anchors ('monsieur', 'vous supplie'); the pencil key on the flap was tested and rejected, and no prior solution was found at the time; Lasry later reported it decoded by Sheila Richards in Secret Writings (1973), so this is an independent re-solution.
outcome.contribution: transcription; key recovered; key extended or corrected
outcome.notes: All three pages transcribed. The letter runs f. 243 -> f. 241; f. 242 (image P2) is the same leaf as f. 243 with the flap down, not a copy (corrected 12 Oct 2026 after WAINUT, PR #30). title: Ferdinand the Catholic to Jerónimo de Vich, Pedrezuela 26 Oct 1515, AHN Estado 8715 N.73 (PARES 12751418)
system.summary: Homophonic letter signs (37 sign types, including letter-pair signs) mixed with three-letter code groups for words, syllables and single letters (159 group types); word values such as que, por, papa, Italia, liga. Not the 1511-12 nomenclator.
system.sibling_key: None found: the 1511-12 key of N.45/N.57/N.60 (targets/vich1511/) and the 1519 system of N.74 (Charles I) are different systems.
system.notes: Symbol runs are short (median 3), so there is little for an n-gram model to hold onto. Clear text: docket 'a 26 de octubre 1515', opening 'videlicet iterum', ending 'en Pedrezuela a xxvj de otubre de dxv'. 197 distinct counts code groups and sign labels together, as transcribed. Structure recovered by Michael Brackx (issue #94, Oct 2026): the code groups stand for syllables and short words inside spelled words as well as for whole words, which is why letter-level annealing failed here in Sept 2026.
conditions.prior_solution.where: Ferdinand's minute of this letter (AGS Estado leg. 847 fol. 125, not digitised) printed in full by Doussinague, La política internacional de Fernando el Católico (1944) p. 520 (not seen, not online), and quoted at length by Terrateig, Política en Italia del Rey Católico (1963) vol. I pp. 631-634 (lines 9-31 of the cipher). A clear draft, not a decipherment: no key was published.
conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie (from the browser developer tools) to the model, set up Claude Code with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal; occasionally offered encouragement or chose which of the model-identified leads to pursue. No target-specific intervention recorded.
conditions.tools: pares.py, lines.py, half.py (in targets/vich1511/); solve73.py, solve73g.py (Spanish 5-gram annealing)
outcome.method_basis: Michael Brackx recovered the sign alphabet ciphertext-only (joint annealing of sign and group values against a Spanish 5-gram, with an encipherment-cost term; no crib) and read 40 code-group types by context (issue #94, 23 Oct 2026); checked on a matched Lazarillo control and by docs/_validate.py (pass). He then found Terrateig 1963 vol. I pp. 631-634 quoting the letter from its minute, used the long quotation as a crib for ll. 9-31 (27 groups read, 11 tentative values confirmed, about 8 corrected) and four context rounds after it. The method stays key recovered from ciphertext-only (the alphabet and the first 40 groups came before the print was found); the code-group extension rests partly on external plaintext. The text is not read: 77 group tokens unread, look-alike readings 3.09% of letters.

title: Filippo Maria Visconti to Francesco Sforza, cipher slips of Nov 1446 - Mar 1447 (BnF italien 1583, 1584; key DECODE R5323)
system.summary: Homophonic substitution (up to six signs a letter) with a full table of vowel+consonant syllable signs, twelve word signs, about fourteen name signs and twelve nulls; no word division; each slip ends with the date, the ducal title in cipher and an alphabet-run padding.
system.sibling_key: The Duke's second key, ASMi cart. 1597 no. 24 (DECODE R5324), reads one slip of the same series (f. 15, targets/visconti1447).
conditions.prior_solution.where: contemporary decipherments on the next leaf of eight of the eleven ital. 1584 letters (ff. 6, 9, 25, 38, 84, 95, 103) and of ital. 1583 f. 130 (f. 131, not digitised); later fair copies of every ital. 1584 letter (ff. 7, 10, 26, 29, 35, 63, 73, 82/85, 92, 101); 19th-c. copies of ital. 1583 ff. 110, 136 and 145 in BnF ital. 1597, made by deciphering the slips. None known for ff. 154 and 158.

title: Filippo Maria Visconti to Francesco Sforza, cipher slips of Nov 1446 - Mar 1447 (BnF italien 1583, 1584; key DECODE R5323)
system.summary: Homophonic substitution (up to six signs a letter) with a full table of vowel+consonant syllable signs, twelve word signs, about fourteen name signs and twelve nulls; no word division; each slip ends with the date, the ducal title in cipher and an alphabet-run padding.
system.sibling_key: The Duke's second key, ASMi cart. 1597 no. 24 (DECODE R5324), reads one slip of the same series (f. 15, targets/visconti1447).
conditions.prior_solution.where: contemporary decipherments on the next leaf of eight of the eleven ital. 1584 letters (ff. 6, 9, 25, 38, 84, 95, 103) and of ital. 1583 f. 130 (f. 131, not digitised); later fair copies of every ital. 1584 letter (ff. 7, 10, 26, 29, 35, 63, 73, 82/85, 92, 101); 19th-c. copies of ital. 1583 ff. 110, 136 and 145 in BnF ital. 1597, made by deciphering the slips. None known for ff. 154 and 158.
conditions.inputs: images; key from archive; cleartext context
conditions.human_role: The project chose the target from the Oct 2026 Venice/Milan sweep and asked for the slips to be read; the model found the key, mapped the volumes, and transcribed and deciphered the slips through worker subagents, checked by the main session.
conditions.tools: Gallica IIIF image API; BnF Archives et manuscrits records (arks); DECODE authenticated record and image download; PIL tiling, deskew and baseline tracking; show-through removal by registered mirror division (f. 110 verso); lang/ Italian word search
outcome.method: read after matching with key from external sources
outcome.method_basis: The key is an unlabelled DECODE key record (ASMi cart. 1597 no. 23, R5323) matched to the slips and checked against two contemporary translations.
outcome.contribution: transcription; catalogue correction; sender or date identified
outcome.verification: contemporary decipherment; independent clear copy; key confirms; historical consistency
outcome.notes: 16637 tokens transcribed, 329 nulls, 1275 unread. Sixteen of the nineteen slips have a decipherment of the time or a later copy (ital. 1584 next to each slip; ital. 1583 ff. 110 and 136 in ital. 1597); only ff. 130, 154 and 158 are deciphered here with no clear text reached. ff. 110 and 136 were merged from a parallel session. f. 15 (key R5324) is written up as visconti1447.

title: Filippo Maria Visconti to Francesco Sforza, cipher slips of Nov 1446 - Mar 1447 (BnF italien 1583, 1584; key DECODE R5323)
system.summary: Homophonic substitution (up to six signs a letter) with a full table of vowel+consonant syllable signs, twelve word signs, about fourteen name signs and twelve nulls; no word division; each slip ends with the date, the ducal title in cipher and an alphabet-run padding.
system.sibling_key: The Duke's second key, ASMi cart. 1597 no. 24 (DECODE R5324), reads one slip of the same series (f. 15, targets/visconti1447).
conditions.prior_solution.where: contemporary decipherments on the next leaf of eight of the eleven ital. 1584 letters (ff. 6, 9, 25, 38, 84, 95, 103) and of ital. 1583 f. 130 (f. 131, not digitised); later fair copies of every ital. 1584 letter (ff. 7, 10, 26, 29, 35, 63, 73, 82/85, 92, 101); 19th-c. copies of ital. 1583 ff. 110, 136 and 145 in BnF ital. 1597, made by deciphering the slips. None known for ff. 154 and 158.
conditions.inputs: images; key from archive; cleartext context
conditions.human_role: The project chose the target from the Oct 2026 Venice/Milan sweep and asked for the slips to be read; the model found the key, mapped the volumes, and transcribed and deciphered the slips through worker subagents, checked by the main session.
conditions.tools: Gallica IIIF image API; BnF Archives et manuscrits records (arks); DECODE authenticated record and image download; PIL tiling, deskew and baseline tracking; show-through removal by registered mirror division (f. 110 verso); lang/ Italian word search
outcome.method: read after matching with key from external sources
outcome.method_basis: The key is an unlabelled DECODE key record (ASMi cart. 1597 no. 23, R5323) matched to the slips and checked against two contemporary translations.
outcome.contribution: transcription; catalogue correction; sender or date identified
outcome.verification: contemporary decipherment; independent clear copy; key confirms; historical consistency
outcome.notes: 16637 tokens transcribed, 329 nulls, 1275 unread. Sixteen of the nineteen slips have a decipherment of the time or a later copy (ital. 1584 next to each slip; ital. 1583 ff. 110 and 136 in ital. 1597); only ff. 130, 154 and 158 are deciphered here with no clear text reached. ff. 110 and 136 were merged from a parallel session. f. 15 (key R5324) is written up as visconti1447.

title: Filippo Maria Visconti to Francesco Sforza, cipher slips of Nov 1446 - Mar 1447 (BnF italien 1583, 1584; key DECODE R5323)
system.summary: Homophonic substitution (up to six signs a letter) with a full table of vowel+consonant syllable signs, twelve word signs, about fourteen name signs and twelve nulls; no word division; each slip ends with the date, the ducal title in cipher and an alphabet-run padding.
system.sibling_key: The Duke's second key, ASMi cart. 1597 no. 24 (DECODE R5324), reads one slip of the same series (f. 15, targets/visconti1447).
conditions.prior_solution.where: contemporary decipherments on the next leaf of eight of the eleven ital. 1584 letters (ff. 6, 9, 25, 38, 84, 95, 103) and of ital. 1583 f. 130 (f. 131, not digitised); later fair copies of every ital. 1584 letter (ff. 7, 10, 26, 29, 35, 63, 73, 82/85, 92, 101); 19th-c. copies of ital. 1583 ff. 110, 136 and 145 in BnF ital. 1597, made by deciphering the slips. None known for ff. 154 and 158.
conditions.inputs: images; key from archive; cleartext context
conditions.human_role: The project chose the target from the Oct 2026 Venice/Milan sweep and asked for the slips to be read; the model found the key, mapped the volumes, and transcribed and deciphered the slips through worker subagents, checked by the main session.
conditions.tools: Gallica IIIF image API; BnF Archives et manuscrits records (arks); DECODE authenticated record and image download; PIL tiling, deskew and baseline tracking; show-through removal by registered mirror division (f. 110 verso); lang/ Italian word search
outcome.method: read after matching with key from external sources
outcome.method_basis: The key is an unlabelled DECODE key record (ASMi cart. 1597 no. 23, R5323) matched to the slips and checked against two contemporary translations.
outcome.contribution: transcription; catalogue correction; sender or date identified
outcome.verification: contemporary decipherment; independent clear copy; key confirms; historical consistency
outcome.notes: 16637 tokens transcribed, 329 nulls, 1275 unread. Sixteen of the nineteen slips have a decipherment of the time or a later copy (ital. 1584 next to each slip; ital. 1583 ff. 110 and 136 in ital. 1597); only ff. 130, 154 and 158 are deciphered here with no clear text reached. ff. 110 and 136 were merged from a parallel session. f. 15 (key R5324) is written up as visconti1447.

system.summary: Homophonic substitution (up to six signs a letter) with a full table of vowel+consonant syllable signs, twelve word signs, about fourteen name signs and twelve nulls; no word division; each slip ends with the date, the ducal title in cipher and an alphabet-run padding.
system.sibling_key: The Duke's second key, ASMi cart. 1597 no. 24 (DECODE R5324), reads one slip of the same series (f. 15, targets/visconti1447).
conditions.prior_solution.where: contemporary decipherments on the next leaf of eight of the eleven ital. 1584 letters (ff. 6, 9, 25, 38, 84, 95, 103) and of ital. 1583 f. 130 (f. 131, not digitised); later fair copies of every ital. 1584 letter (ff. 7, 10, 26, 29, 35, 63, 73, 82/85, 92, 101); 19th-c. copies of ital. 1583 ff. 110, 136 and 145 in BnF ital. 1597, made by deciphering the slips. None known for ff. 154 and 158.

title: Filippo Maria Visconti to Francesco Sforza, cipher slips of Nov 1446 - Mar 1447 (BnF italien 1583, 1584; key DECODE R5323)
system.summary: Homophonic substitution (up to six signs a letter) with a full table of vowel+consonant syllable signs, twelve word signs, about fourteen name signs and twelve nulls; no word division; each slip ends with the date, the ducal title in cipher and an alphabet-run padding.
system.sibling_key: The Duke's second key, ASMi cart. 1597 no. 24 (DECODE R5324), reads one slip of the same series (f. 15, targets/visconti1447).
conditions.prior_solution.where: contemporary decipherments on the next leaf of eight of the eleven ital. 1584 letters (ff. 6, 9, 25, 38, 84, 95, 103) and of ital. 1583 f. 130 (f. 131, not digitised); later fair copies of every ital. 1584 letter (ff. 7, 10, 26, 29, 35, 63, 73, 82/85, 92, 101); 19th-c. copies of ital. 1583 ff. 110, 136 and 145 in BnF ital. 1597, made by deciphering the slips. None known for ff. 154 and 158.

title: Filippo Maria Visconti to Francesco Sforza, cipher slips of Nov 1446 - Mar 1447 (BnF italien 1583, 1584; key DECODE R5323)
system.summary: Homophonic substitution (up to six signs a letter) with a full table of vowel+consonant syllable signs, twelve word signs, about fourteen name signs and twelve nulls; no word division; each slip ends with the date, the ducal title in cipher and an alphabet-run padding.
system.sibling_key: The Duke's second key, ASMi cart. 1597 no. 24 (DECODE R5324), reads one slip of the same series (f. 15, targets/visconti1447).
conditions.prior_solution.where: contemporary decipherments on the next leaf of eight of the eleven ital. 1584 letters (ff. 6, 9, 25, 38, 84, 95, 103) and of ital. 1583 f. 130 (f. 131, not digitised); later fair copies of every ital. 1584 letter (ff. 7, 10, 26, 29, 35, 63, 73, 82/85, 92, 101); 19th-c. copies of ital. 1583 ff. 110, 136 and 145 in BnF ital. 1597, made by deciphering the slips. None known for ff. 154 and 158.
conditions.inputs: images; key from archive; cleartext context
conditions.human_role: The project chose the target from the Oct 2026 Venice/Milan sweep and asked for the slips to be read; the model found the key, mapped the volumes, and transcribed and deciphered the slips through worker subagents, checked by the main session.

outcome.method_basis: The key is an unlabelled DECODE key record (ASMi cart. 1597 no. 23, R5323) matched to the slips and checked against two contemporary translations.

system.summary: Homophonic substitution (up to six signs a letter) with a full table of vowel+consonant syllable signs, twelve word signs, about fourteen name signs and twelve nulls; no word division; each slip ends with the date, the ducal title in cipher and an alphabet-run padding.

None known for ff. 154 and 158.

title: John Wood to Cecil, 6 September 1568: the cipher line on BL Add MS 4136 f. 33 (DECODE R2989; catalogue 97)
system.summary: One line of 39 symbols in the family of the Moray-Wood 1568 cipher (x and z variants, g, o, e, f), probably a letter substitution.
system.sibling_key: Moray to Wood, 13 July 1568 (Tomokiyo's transcription, unread): same symbol families, not aligned glyph for glyph
system.notes: IC 0.069 on 39 symbols; opens and closes with the same trigram g x ob. The Throckmorton text on the same leaf (Cipher 3) and the f. 32 margin code are other systems with their own entries.
conditions.prior_solution.where: Tomokiyo, cryptiana unsolved.htm, lists it as unidentified; Bain ii 804 prints the letter with one phrase marked as cipher, which does not align with this line
conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie (from the browser developer tools) to the model, set up Claude Code with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal; occasionally offered encouragement or chose which of the model-identified leads to pursue. conditions.tools: crib alignment search (align3.py, align4.py)
outcome.method_basis: Bain's printed cipher phrase does not align with the 39-symbol line under any tested model, and a non-uniqueness test shows that dozens of unrelated English readings fit it, so it is undetermined by its own text.
outcome.notes: Attempted, closed unread 21 Sept 2026. Needs the Hatfield original (Cecil Papers vol. 1) for a true crib. Split 14 Oct 2026 from wod1568.
